info.title: DataSportsAPI
info.summary: Real-time sports data over REST for 24 sports — scores, schedules, lineups, match statistics, tables, and team, player and league profiles.
info.description:
One consistent JSON contract for 24 sports: fixtures and live scores, lineups and statistics, standings, plus teams, players and leagues, delivered in real time over REST, WebSocket and webhooks.

Successful responses use a `{ data, meta? }` envelope; failures return `{ error: { code, message } }` under a matching HTTP status. All ids are DataSportsAPI ids. Each component schema documents its fields, units and enum values, as does the data reference (https://datasportsapi.com/markdown/reference.md). The WebSocket stream, webhooks and widgets are documented at https://datasportsapi.com/docs/.

Availability: live. During the beta the Free plan allows 1,000 requests a day (100 a day after).

tags.name: livescores
tags.description: Live scores. Fixtures that are in play right now. If you are building a live feature, the WebSocket is the better fit: it delivers the same objects and then pushes deltas.

tags.name: fixtures
tags.description: Fixtures. Look up fixtures by date, or fetch one match together with its detail sub-resources.

tags.name: discovery
tags.description: Discovery. Starting points for finding ids: world rankings, plus the full set of a sport’s leagues by country or by category.

tags.name: races
tags.description: Race sports. Motorsport and cycling — the sports with kind races in /v2/sports. Here a series takes the place of a league (Formula 1, MotoGP; in cycling, the full men’s or women’s calendar). Each race is either a Grand Prix weekend or one cycling race, split into sessions — the timed parts such as practice, qualifying, a sprint, the race itself or a cycling stage. Drivers and riders, like their teams, are TeamRefs, which /v2/teams/{id} resolves. Times are always in milliseconds and distances in metres. The WebSocket does not carry these sports yet; while a session runs, poll /v2/races/{id} and its /results.

tags.name: people
tags.description: Referees & managers. Fixture.referee carries referee ids; TeamDetail.manager and Fixture.homeManager / awayManager carry manager ids. Both kinds can also be found through /v2/search.

tags.name: venues
tags.description: Venues. Venue ids appear on Fixture.venue and TeamDetail.venue, and /v2/search can look venues up too.

tags.name: odds
tags.description: Betting odds. Prices from one bookmaker, supplied through our data source, both before kick-off and in play, available since 2026-11-04; the odds carry no bookmaker identity. Odds live exclusively on dedicated endpoints and a dedicated WebSocket channel: fixtures, lists and deltas never include betting fields, so your match data contains no odds unless you request them. Included in the Pro, Business and Enterprise plans, with live prices on odds:{id} for Business and Enterprise accounts. Odds are third-party prices provided for information only — neither betting advice nor an offer to place a bet; make sure you follow the rules on displaying betting odds wherever your users are.

tags.name: tracking
tags.description: Tracking data. Positional data for a match, available since 2026-11-12 with history back to 2026-11-07. Football gets a live ball track and live events — goals, shots, cards, substitutions and set pieces seconds after they happen, plus the flow of play (ball safe, attack, dangerous attack, change of possession) — and, after the match, the full event list with positions and passes. Tennis gets every serve and point plus live positions of the ball and the players. Basketball and ice hockey get a match timeline with shot spots, filled live since 2026-11-13 (basketball also keeps its post-match events); darts gets a live timeline of every dart and every visit (since 2026-11-13); and NBA games add the live positions of all ten players and the ball, five times a second (since 2026-11-13). Enterprise plan only: the REST endpoints are below, and the tracking:{id} WebSocket channel streams the same data live. Every position is in the fixture’s coordinate frame (TrackingSummary.coordinates) — 0–100 for football, basketball and ice hockey, with the home side attacking towards x = 100 for the whole match, millimetres from the middle of the net for tennis, and none for darts, where each dart names the bed it hit instead. Players are identified by name from the match squad, without an id.

tags.name: exports
tags.description: Bulk exports. For the Business and Enterprise plans. Get a whole league season as files: create an export, poll its status, then download. Exports are generated in the background from the same data the endpoints above serve; each account may create up to 20 per UTC day, and each one is kept for 7 days. Business reads one year back, so a season that ended before that window is refused (403 history_not_in_plan) on that plan.

tags.name: websocket
tags.description: WebSocket. Live deltas for scores and statuses. Obtain a single-use ticket via REST and then open the connection, so your API key never appears in a WebSocket URL. Offered on Business (three simultaneous connections per account) and Enterprise (five), with the tracking:{id} channel kept for Enterprise.

get.description:
Lists all supported sports, each with the number of matches live right now. Matches the source has left open — 45 min without any change, with a kick-off further back than a match in that sport could run — do not count towards it. kind tells you which endpoint family serves the sport: fixtures, for sports served by the Fixtures, Teams and Leagues endpoints; races, for motorsport and cycling, which the Race sports endpoints cover (their fixture lists stay empty).

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
Coverage figures for the whole API in one call, open to every plan: entity totals, each sport’s league directory and how far back its headline competitions reach. The totals object counts how many teams, players, fixtures, leagues, seasons, venues, managers and referees have a DataSportsAPI id; each one can be fetched by that id, and the numbers never go down. The bySport list describes every sport’s directory — its categories (countries, tours, regions or games) with the leagues they hold, or the series for motorsport and cycling — together with up to ten headline competitions, each with its number of seasons and its first season; historyFrom is the earliest of those. The history object condenses the depth of all headline competitions into a median span in years and the oldest season. Old seasons are thinner than recent ones: results and tables usually go back further than lineups and statistics. updatedAt says when the figures were computed — totals every hour, directories once a day. A sport may be absent for a while after a restart, until its directory has been read again, and until the very first count is ready the endpoint answers 503 with Retry-After.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

Returns every live fixture across all sports, or one sport’s in-play board when ?sport= is set; each match reflects the live index, so its state is identical to the unfiltered call and to the WebSocket. Stale entries — no change for 45 min, and a start further back than a match in that sport can run — are dropped both here and on the WebSocket.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
Recent moments from the livescores channel, newest first, reaching back 7 days: score changes of any kind (goals, baskets, sets and runs, including corrections that lowered a score), red cards, kick-offs, period starts, breaks and final whistles. Every moment carries the score and status as they stood just after it, plus the ids and names of both sides, which is enough to fill a ticker before the WebSocket has delivered anything, or to show a client what happened while it was away for longer than replay covers. Each moment has exactly one kind, the first that fits in the order score, redCard, finished, break, kickoff, period. Available since 2026-11-16.

**Note:** Nothing older than 7 days is kept. The moments are recorded from the same changes the livescores channel publishes, as we publish them, and at is that publication time. To combine them with live deltas, match on fixtureId + kind + score.

**Plans:** Business and up; other plans receive 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

get.description:
Fixtures starting on one UTC date, for a single league, one category (country, region or tour, all its leagues at once), one country in a sport, or a whole sport paged ten leagues at a time by league rank.

**Note:** Need a single country’s schedule, amateur and youth competitions included? Pass category= (take the id from that day’s /v2/fixtures/counts?sport= or from /v2/categories), or combine sport= with country=; either returns everything in one request rather than paging through the sport. When only sport is set, keep requesting pages until hasNextPage is false. All pages except the final one contain 10 leagues, so an empty page tells you the day is exhausted; a page may still carry fewer fixtures than leagues, because a league whose matches sit just outside the UTC day adds nothing. The set of fixtures for a date is cached — for minutes on today and future dates, for hours on past dates, and permanently once every fixture has finished — whereas the status, score and clock of a live fixture are accurate to the second (details in Data freshness). If you need a live feed, /v2/livescores or the WebSocket is the better fit.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: UTC date as YYYY-MM-DD, from 1990-01-01 to one year in the future

parameters.name: sport
parameters.description: sport slug; mandatory when neither league nor category is set

parameters.name: league
parameters.description: league id — returns only that league’s fixtures for the date, on a single page (page has to be 0)

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: category id, as listed by /v2/categories or /v2/fixtures/counts — all leagues of that country, region or tour for the date, sorted by start time, on a single page (page has to be 0). Available since 2026-11-04

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: two-letter Country.code (EN, ES, US …; case-insensitive), used together with sport — returns the date’s fixtures from that country’s categories in the sport, on a single page. Available since 2026-11-04

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: only when sport is the sole filter: page index 0–99 (defaults to 0), each page covering 10 leagues

meta.description: date, page, count, hasNextPage; the league filter adds league (and sport when passed), with page fixed at 0 and hasNextPage false; the category filter adds category (and sport when passed), single page; the country filter adds sport, country, categoryIds (the categories that were queried), complete; sport on its own adds sport, leagueCount (number of leagues on this page), complete (false if some league lists were temporarily unavailable — try again shortly)

get.description:
Fixture totals for a UTC date without paging: given a sport, the date’s total and a row per category (country, region, tour) with fixture and league counts, for any date; with no sport, today’s total per sport. The liveCount field gives the number of matches currently in play.

**Note:** Dates are UTC, as on /v2/fixtures. liveCount is filled for today only (null on other dates) and comes from our live index — identical to the figure on /v2/sports — rather than from the date’s list, so a match that began yesterday may be included. Categories are sorted by fixture count, largest first; there is no live count per category because the source does not track one. With sport, fixtureCount is the sum across categories; without sport, it is the sum across sports. For one sport these totals may diverge by a few percent, since the category list includes some matches spilling over from late on the previous day. Race sports (motorsport, cycling) have no categories on this endpoint — use /v2/races. Available on all plans.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
One fixture in full: both teams, score, status, match clock, winner, league, season, round, venue, the referee (career cards per game), the two managers (homeManager / awayManager) and previousLegFixtureId. That field holds our id for the first leg or the previous game in a series, and on a completed second leg aggregateWinner names the side that went through. Some sports add more: seeds (homeSeed / awaySeed); in tennis, surface (hard / clay / grass / carpet, indoor), discipline (singles or doubles) and serving (who is serving at the moment); in darts, servedFirst (the side that threw the opening dart of the match); in cricket, battingSide, note, toss (winner, bat / bowl), tvUmpire and umpires; in MMA and boxing, fightResult (method, round and, for a stoppage, the time), fightCard (main card / prelims, order, weight class) and fightDiscipline (boxing, kickboxing, muayThai, …, if the source tags one); attendance (spectators, when reported); matchFormat (best of sets / legs in darts, best of games in esports); in baseball, inningState (inning, top / bottom, outs, count, runners); in basketball, timeouts (left per side) and bonus (which sides are in the bonus); in American football, downAndDistance (down, yards to go, field position, possession, play type); in football, varCheck (a VAR review in progress and the side it concerns); finalResultOnly (true when the source has nothing beyond the result); and, in set or round sports, durations (seconds per completed set or round, plus the total).

**Note:** All score components live under periods: extra time in football and futsal is periods.extra1 / extra2, overtime in any other sport is periods.overtime, and extra innings in baseball are period10, period11, and so on. A shoot-out is never part of current — it goes in penalties — except that in ice hockey current includes the single goal awarded for winning a shoot-out. status.description is our own label, e.g. “Game 1”, “After overtime”, “After extra time” or “After penalties”. When the source drops coverage of a fixture, its status becomes canceled and both score sides are empty. For a match decided on penalties, winner is the shoot-out winner — second legs included, where the result on the night remains in normalTime; aggregateWinner names the side that progressed on aggregate (null if the source leaves a level aggregate unresolved). Lists and WebSocket snapshots may show aggregateWinner as null, so take it from this endpoint. Only this endpoint fills referee, homeManager / awayManager, previousLegFixtureId, toss, umpires, tvUmpire, fightCard and attendance; in fixture lists, on the live board and in WebSocket snapshots they are null (surface is filled here and on the live tennis board as well). inningState, timeouts, bonus, downAndDistance and varCheck exist only during play and are null at any other time. Every one of them except bonus is pushed in WebSocket deltas — inningState and varCheck as whole objects, timeouts and downAndDistance as partial updates (whole on first appearance, null once play stops). Because the source resends the baseball state roughly once a minute, the count may trail the action. durations — filled for tennis and the other set sports and for MMA rounds, null elsewhere — gains one period each time a set finishes, which is also delivered in WebSocket deltas (the completed period plus the updated totalSeconds; the set in progress began at clock.periodStartedAt). fightResult comes in a separate WebSocket delta, normally after the one that ends the fight, because the source publishes it only 20–60 s after the winner is known. In rugby, periods fill in live: period1 at half-time, then period2 = current − period1 through the second half. Esports periods: CS records 1 for each map won and 0 otherwise; LoL records how many kills the side made in game N. serving replaces firstToServe, which carries the same value and is deprecated but still present for now.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
Team lineups and formations plus unavailable players, with every player carrying a match rating and statistics.

**Note:** How much you get depends on the fixture: top leagues come with lineups plus per-player ratings and statistics, while many youth, amateur and friendly matches never receive any. Player statistics reuse the team-statistics keys wherever the meaning matches (passes, accuratePasses, shotsOnGoal, tackles, …; bigChancesCreated counts big chances the player set up for a teammate). Each …Percentage field is a share from 0 to 100, with one exception: basketball’s trueShootingPercentage can exceed 100 (for example a handful of free throws plus a three). Players who did not take part have rating and statistics set to null; avgRating (football) holds the player’s season average and is filled mainly before and around kick-off. The profile fields heightCm, dateOfBirth, country and marketValue mirror the player’s profile (/v2/players/{id}) and are null when the source has no value — common in predicted lineups — with marketValue largely limited to football. Preferred foot is missing because the lineups we receive lack it; the profile and the squad have it. position is a sport-dependent word (G means goalkeeper in football, goalie in ice hockey and guard in basketball), while positionCode retains the source’s letter. A fixture without lineups (so far) answers 200 with confirmed: false and both sides empty; only an unknown id gets 404. While a match is live, the data is refreshed roughly every 30 seconds.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
Team statistics for the match, organised by period and by category.

**Note:** Coverage is graded the same way as for lineups and grows richer as the match goes on: a lower-tier fixture might offer nothing but cards, whereas a top league delivers every group. Statistic keys form one shared vocabulary across all sports (totalShots, shotsOnGoal, passes, fouls, …; the reference’s Statistic keys lists every key per sport), and group keys follow a fixed table for each sport. In American football, the team-level passingNetYards and passingYardsPerAttempt are gross figures from the source (sacks are not subtracted), whereas a player’s passingNetYards in the lineups is net. A fixture without statistics (yet — before kick-off, for instance) returns 200 with { "periods": [] }; you only get 404 for an id that does not exist. Data is refreshed approximately every 30 seconds during a live match.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
The match’s incidents in chronological order, oldest first: goals, cards, substitutions, period markers and added-time announcements.

**Note:** Returns an empty array if the fixture has no events (yet). For an injuryTime incident, addedMinute holds the number of added minutes announced. minute is null whenever the clock is not running — before kick-off, at half-time, for bench events and during a shoot-out. Shoot-out kicks are listed last, in the order taken: shootoutSequence numbers them 1…N across both sides, and shootoutRound gives the kick’s position (1st, 2nd, …) within the taker’s side. A period row marks the end of a period: its period is the one just completed, so the period currently in progress has no row; in set sports its homeScore / awayScore are the sets won up to that point. period is filled on every incident. All fields appear on every incident, set to null where irrelevant to the type, and type and detail are closed enums. Football goals carry buildUp, the chain of actions that led to the goal — shots (saved, missed, off the woodwork, penalties saved or missed), passes, crosses, free kicks, tackles, interceptions and clearances — each step with its side, player and minute, start and end pitch positions, assist, body part and expected goals, and the goal itself as the last step; buildUp is [] on all other incidents and when the source provides none. Cricket ball-by-ball and the point-level rows of set sports are not part of this list. Refreshed about every 30 seconds during a live match.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

Text commentary from the source, one action per entry, oldest first, in football (cards, shots, corners, substitutions and more, by minute) and basketball (each basket, free throw, rebound, foul and turnover). Basketball entries also give the game clock, the running score, the basket’s value and its location on the court.

**Note:** The English text is produced by the source’s data provider and is separate from our AI commentary, which lives at /commentary. type is a closed enum, with other covering anything we have not mapped. Each entry includes every field, null where it does not apply: football uses minute / addedMinute; basketball uses periodSecond (seconds gone in the period), periodSecondsLeft (what the game clock shows), at, position / zone on the court, and scoreType on scoreChange; homeScore / awayScore appear on scoreChange (and on a football penaltyScored, carried forward from the previous goal). If the source has no commentary, the array is empty.

**Plans:** Requires Pro, Business or Enterprise; a Free or Starter key receives 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

Attack-momentum curve (football, plus any other sport where the source draws one) with a point for every minute: positive values mean home pressure, negative values away pressure. get.description:
DataSportsAPI’s in-house win probabilities for a football fixture: a pre-match estimate, the live home / draw / away split and a curve with a point at kick-off, one per minute and one right after each goal. Red cards, the start or end of a period and big missed chances (reason bigChance) add a point too, and every point is stamped with the UTC instant it refers to (at). Available on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans.

**Note:** This is an analytical indicator, not betting advice, and no bookmaker odds feed into it. The model is at v3 (since 2026-10-25; v2 dated from 2026-10-22) and works openly as follows. Pre-match expected goals for each side combine three inputs. First, each team’s last 30 results in every competition, league and European cups alike, with each result weighted by how strong the opponent was. Second, the team’s domestic league table — goals scored and conceded per game, pulled towards the league average. Third, our league-strength coefficients, estimated from three seasons of European cup matches, so that teams from different leagues share one scale. The result is then mixed with three more signals: the table of the current competition, which gains weight as it fills up (after two games of a European campaign overall strength still dominates; after 30 league games the table does), the latest five results, and home advantage, which is zero in a final. On a backtest held out by season (over 8,000 league matches and 1,500 European ones) this beat v1 on both sets, with the biggest improvement in European ties and in the opening weeks of a season. v3 adds one exception: when a league match involves a newcomer — a side that arrived in the competition by promotion or relegation, early in the season — only the current table and form are used, because the newcomer’s strength measured on its previous league’s scale distorted the estimate. A fixture whose pre-match estimate was set under an earlier model stays on that model (v1 and v2 use the same in-play logic). During play, each side’s remaining goals follow a Poisson distribution over the time left (added time included, with goals becoming more likely as the match progresses); the rate drops for a team reduced to ten men (and rises for its opponent) and is tilted for the following half hour by the previous ten minutes of attack momentum. These constants were fitted on 1,080 completed matches from 12 competitions and validated on the subsequent season. From v3 onwards the in-play result is calibrated — made slightly less confident, since the curve proved a little over-confident on that backtest — and this calibration ramps in across the first 15 minutes so that the kick-off point matches the pre-match estimate. Live expected goals from the shot map are left out of the scoring rate, as they added nothing measurable on that backtest; a big missed chance does, however, still add a point to the curve. home + draw + away = 1, and draw means the scores are level at the end, counting extra time but not a shoot-out. Ahead of kick-off the response holds the pre-match estimate with an empty series; after the final whistle it holds 1 / 0 / 0 and the complete curve, which is stored for good. The pre-match estimate is frozen as soon as the match begins. Each point has an at timestamp for the match moment it stands for — the close of that minute, or the goal or whistle itself — read from the running match clock or, failing that, estimated from kick-off assuming a 15-minute half-time; Along the curve, at only ever goes up. current.at records when the estimate was computed (for a finished match, the end of the match). Points are saved once they are two minutes old and are never altered afterwards, so the curve reflects what the model said in the moment. When polling, set since to your latest at minus two minutes (a late-listed event from the source can still add a point within the most recent two minutes) and overwrite your points after since with the response. For push updates, fixture:{id} WebSocket channels on Business and Enterprise receive a winProbability frame whenever any outcome shifts by one percentage point or more.

**Plans:** Requires Pro, Business or Enterprise; a Free or Starter key receives 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

get.description:
In-game win probability as published by our data source (not DataSportsAPI’s model): home and away values for each minute of play. Limited to American football (NFL), the only sport for which the source provides it. Available on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans.

**Note:** The model field always reads "source": the figure comes with the source’s match data, and we do not know how it is calculated. For our own model see /v2/fixtures/{id}/win-probability (football only, models v1 to v3). Treat it as an analytical indicator, not betting advice. minute counts playing time (15 per NFL quarter, with overtime continuing the sequence), at roughly one point per minute; individual minutes may be absent and the curve may begin at 1. The last point is just the source’s final estimate; it is not forced to 1 / 0 when the game ends. Ties are not modelled, so home + away = 1. Any other sport, or a game without source data, returns 200 with an empty series and the period figures set to null. There is no WebSocket frame for it; over REST, polling about every 30 seconds during play is enough.

**Plans:** Requires Pro, Business or Enterprise; a Free or Starter key receives 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

AI-written commentary on a football fixture, oldest first by seq (newest 100): a short entry per goal, missed penalty, red card, VAR decision, period start or end, big chance and sustained swing in momentum. Events seconds apart are merged into one entry, and there are summaries at half-time and full time. Available on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans.

**Note:** DataSportsAPI AI writes every line from our own match data alone (score, clock, events, statistics, shot map and our win-probability model) and stays clear of betting language. Entries are generated only while the match is being followed, either through this endpoint or through a fixture:{id} WebSocket channel, so request it while the game is on; a match that nobody followed has no entries. Featured top-league matches on datasportsapi.com always get commentary. Every entry is written a single time and served identically to all clients, and its seq is permanent. kind takes one of these values: kickoff, goal, redCard, missedPenalty, varDecision, bigChance, momentum, periodStart, periodEnd, halfTime, fullTime, update. The minute of a fullTime summary is 90 (120 after extra time). On Business and Enterprise, fixture:{id} channels receive a commentary frame for each new entry.

**Plans:** Requires Pro, Business or Enterprise; a Free or Starter key receives 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

get.description:
All shots, oldest first, with outcome and expected goals; football gives expectedGoals / expectedGoalsOnTarget, pitch and goal-mouth coordinates, body part and situation, ice hockey technique and strength. Ice hockey shots also carry rink coordinates; basketball lists each field-goal attempt as made, missed or blocked along with its court location.

**Note:** Available for football, ice hockey and basketball in covered leagues; any other case returns an empty array. In football and ice hockey, outcome is goal | save | miss | block | post, and a football shot cleared off the line counts as a block. In basketball the outcomes are goal (made), miss and block; positions are measured from the basket in tenths of a foot, the player and time fields are null, and every home shot comes before the away shots. Only ice hockey uses technique (wrist, snap, slap, …) and strength. goalType is regular, ownGoal or penalty. Shoot-out kicks appear at the end: shootoutSequence is the order of kicks across both teams (matching the events), and shootoutRound is the kick’s number (1st, 2nd, …) for the taker’s side. In football, period (since 2026-10-24; null for earlier data) is derived from the minute: period1, period2, extra1, extra2, or penalties for a shoot-out kick. While a match is live the list is re-read about every 30 seconds; fixture:{id} WebSocket channels (Business and Enterprise) receive the entire list as a shotmap frame whenever it changes.

**Plans:** Requires Pro, Business or Enterprise; a Free or Starter key receives 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

get.description:
A point-by-point breakdown of the match. Tennis nests sets → games (server, winner, set score) → points; badminton, table tennis and volleyball nest sets → rallies, with the running score. Cricket nests innings → overs → balls: each ball has its batter, bowler, outcome, runs, extras, wicket and dismissal, and the score after the delivery, and since 2026-11-04 also the source’s commentary text for each ball, the wagon wheel (zone, angle and distance of the shot) and the pitching spot. Baseball lists at-bats with inning, top / bottom, batting side, batter and pitcher, plus the home side’s win probability before and after the at-bat. Darts nests sets → legs (starting score, first thrower, winner, checkout) → visits (visit score, both sides’ remaining totals, checkout).

**Note:** format names the one list that holds data (tennis and rally sports: sets; cricket: innings; baseball: atBats; darts: darts); every other list is empty. Darts visits do not break down into individual darts, as the source has none; a match played in legs is represented as a single set. On cricket balls (since 2026-11-04), commentary carries the source’s English text (null below the top tiers). shot describes the wagon wheel: zone is the fielding sector, as seen for a right-handed batter ( squareLeg, fineLeg, behindWicket, thirdMan, point, coverPoint, cover, longOff, straight, longOn, midWicket), angle in degrees (0 square leg, 90 behind the keeper, 180 point, 270 straight) and distance on a 1–5 scale (5 = reached the boundary); it is null when the batter did not hit the ball. pitchedAt gives where the ball pitched, in the source’s own units, with y growing with distance from the batter (about 25 for a yorker, 41 for a good length, 54 for a short ball). Each baseball at-bat includes the source’s home win probability (0–100, separate from our model) and, since 2026-11-04, an id you can pass to /v2/fixtures/{id}/at-bats/{atBatId}/pitches, where the last pitch listed ends the at-bat with its result. Any other sport, or a match with no point-by-point data yet, gets 200 with format null and every list empty. For rally sports you only get the rallies the source captured; lower tiers may skip some, which shows up as a jump in the running score. Each tennis point holds the score after it (homeScore / awayScore such as "15" or "A"; null on the game-winning point added at the end), a description (ace or doubleFault) and homeType / awayType (one of won, breakPoint, setPoint, miniBreak, none). In a match tie-break, the deciding set holds it as its only game, played to 10. Refreshed about every 30 seconds during a live match.

**Plans:** Requires Pro, Business or Enterprise; a Free or Starter key receives 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

get.description:
Full cricket scorecard by innings: total, extras, batting card (runs, balls, fours, sixes, strike rate, state, dismissal, bowler, fielder) and bowling card (overs, maidens, runs, wickets, economy, wides, no-balls). Falls of wicket and partnerships follow.

**Note:** Any other sport, or a cricket match before the first delivery, returns 200 with an empty innings list. Overs follow cricket notation, so 19.3 is 19 overs plus 3 balls; once an over is complete the figure moves up to the next whole number (5 rather than the source’s 4.6), and the same goes for falls of wicket. Partnerships are frequently missing for multi-day matches. Refreshed about every 30 seconds during a live match. current (CricketState) describes the crease in the live innings — striker, non-striker, bowler, over and ball — which we compute from the ball-by-ball data instead of relying on the source’s unreliable current-batsman field. It is null when no innings is under way or the match lacks ball-by-ball coverage, and right after a delivery its batters can briefly read null until the ball-by-ball data and the scorecard agree again. The only ambiguous case is a run out, where it is unclear at which end the batter was dismissed.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
Esports only: the series game by game, each with status, map, start time, duration, winner and, for each side, its score and its players (role, champion / hero, kills, deaths, assists and per-title figures). Those figures are League of Legends gold, creep score and level; Dota 2 net worth, last hits, denies, and gold and experience per minute; Counter-Strike KAST, ADR, K − D, headshot kills, first-kill difference and flash assists. Each side also lists bans and objectives (towers, dragons — broken down by element for League of Legends in dragonsByType —, barons, barracks, …). Since 2026-11-04 Counter-Strike also has a record per round: who won it, the way it ended (elimination, bomb defused, bomb exploded, time expired), the side (CT / T) the home team played, and the side it started on.

**Note:** Any other sport returns 200 with an empty array. Single-map titles (League of Legends) have map set to null. The title decides which player and objective fields carry values: gold, dragons and barons belong to League of Legends; denies, netWorth, goldPerMinute, experiencePerMinute, barracks and firstBlood to Dota 2; averageDamagePerRound, headshotKills, kastPercentage, killDeathDifference, firstKillDifference and flashAssists to Counter-Strike. Fields the source does not track for a title are null. Counter-Strike has neither bans nor objectives, and a map still being played has no lineup — its figures show up a few minutes after the map finishes. rounds is empty for every other title; on a Counter-Strike map it fills up as rounds are completed, with overtime rounds carrying on the numbering and flagged overtime: true, while roundsPerHalf / overtimeRoundsPerHalf define the halves.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
Baseball only: one at-bat pitch by pitch — type (MLB Statcast categories: four-seam fastball, sinker, cutter, changeup, curveball, slider, sweeper, …), zone, release speed, result, count and outs after each. Each pitch also carries the score, the batted ball (trajectory, hardness) and what the runners and fielders did. Plays that happen between pitches, such as a stolen-base attempt, appear as rows with kind steal.

**Note:** Other sports get 200 and an empty array. balls / strikes / outs reflect the count AFTER the pitch, and the final pitch (endsAtBat true) carries the at-bat’s result as its outcome. outcome comes from a closed set; when it is other, outcomeCode holds the source’s own code. zone follows MLB Statcast numbering (1–9 inside the strike zone, 11–14 outside it). speedKmh holds the release speed in km/h; multiply it by 0.6214 for mph. For runners, fromBase 0 is the batter, toBase 4 means a run scored, and toBase is null when the runner was put out. Lists saved before 2026-11-04 show AtBat.id as null until they are refreshed.

**Plans:** Requires Pro, Business or Enterprise; a Free or Starter key receives 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

get.description:
Returns one page of a team’s fixtures, either recent or upcoming.

**Note:** If the team exists but has nothing to list, the response is 200 with an empty array. Since 2026-10-24 every competitor list splits matches the same way. upcoming holds matches not yet started (including ones postponed to a future date), soonest first, and page 0 also includes a next match that the source has filed under recent (tennis players, fighters). recent holds live, finished and called-off matches, with the newest at the top of every page. For a live or just-finished match, status, score and clock are accurate to the second. Once a match kicks off it moves to recent on your next request, and both lists are rebuilt on the first request after any of the team’s matches ends, is rescheduled or is postponed (see Data freshness).

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
A feed of the newest football transfers from all leagues, 50 per page, built from the same Transfer objects as team transfer lists. Order it by date (newest move first), by fee (largest first) or by player popularity, Filters narrow it to one league (moves to or from its clubs), a position, a nationality and an age range.

**Note:** Covers football alone, the only sport for which the source maintains this feed. latest orders moves by the date they take effect, which means a loan expiring today is listed next to a signing announced today. Releases and moves into free agency end at "No team" — to stays null and toName holds that label. The feed updates every 30 minutes.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
League tables for a single season. With no extra parameters you get the one table marked primary for the season — the league table, or in a group stage the first group; meta.overall tells you whether it includes every team. Add group=all to get every table (conferences, divisions, groups), or type=home / type=away for a table built from home or away games alone.

**Note:** A season may hold several tables, listed in our data source’s order — for example two conferences, four divisions and a league table in the NHL, two conferences and an overall table in MLS, and one table per group at a World Cup. Exactly one table is flagged primary and served by default — the league table if there is one, otherwise the largest table, and the first group when all are the same size. overall is true solely for a table that contains every team in the season. position always runs 1..n; we re-rank rows whenever the source’s numbering does not. A column that does not apply to a sport is null — the NBA ranks on winPercentage, so its points column is null; draws is null in any table where a draw is impossible (basketball, ice hockey, baseball, volleyball, …); overtimeLosses is filled in ice hockey; scoresFor / scoresAgainst are measured in scoreUnit (goals, points, runs, sets, …); streak (+3 means three straight wins, −2 two straight losses) appears where the source provides it (NBA, EuroLeague, Liga ACB, …). form, added on 2026-10-24, lists up to five of the team’s most recent results in this competition season, oldest first — only home or only away results in the home / away tables — and is null where the source has none. Football publishes split home / away tables, and so do a number of basketball, handball, volleyball and ice-hockey competitions — the KHL, the SuperLega, Liga ACB, the EuroLeague and the Handball-Bundesliga among them. The NBA and NHL publish none and the NFL stops updating its versions, so for those three sports (basketball, ice hockey, American football) we compute them ourselves (meta.source computed) from the finished regular-season fixtures: a home row counts only home games, an away row only away games. They carry only the columns that the same method, run over every game, reproduces exactly for the overall table (NBA: wins, losses, winPercentage, gamesBehind within each table, scores; NFL: wins, losses, draws, winPercentage, scores; NHL: wins, losses, overtimeLosses — defeats in overtime or a shoot-out — and points at 2 per win plus 1 per overtime loss, scores). In those sports a published home / away table that lacks games is swapped for the computed one. In winPercentage a tie is worth half a win. Rows are ordered by points or win share, with ties broken by wins and then score difference — head-to-head is never used. Updated once a day.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
A race’s classification — in motorsport the main race session (the last of type race) with grid, pit stops, tyre stints, the set now fitted (currentTyre: compound, new or used), inPit, best laps and points. That session is named in meta.session, and inPit is true while the car sits in the pit lane during a running session. For a cycling stage race it is the general classification, with every rider’s secondary classifications (points, mountains, young rider, jersey). Pass session= to get a single session instead (a practice, a qualifying, a stage) or a single qualifying part (Q1, Q2…). Where our data source stores a knock-out qualifying only part by part (MotoGP), we merge the parts into the series’ own ranking: the Q2 riders first in their Q2 order, then the Q1 riders who did not advance in their Q1 order, with the places counting on; every line states which part it comes from.

**Note:** state is one of classified, didNotFinish, didNotStart, disqualified or notClassified. Anyone outside the classification has position null, and our data source may also skip a place. timeMs holds the total time for a race or stage, or the best lap for practice and qualifying. For lapped competitors (see lapsBehind), for those who are out and for classified riders whose time the source did not record (cycling), timeMs, gapMs and intervalMs are null. tyreStints is filled for Formula 1 races only; cycling is null except on the overall result of a stage race. Only a qualifying merged from its parts has part ("Q2", "Q1"). In that case timeMs / gapMs / intervalMs refer to that part (best lap, gap to the part’s fastest), lines without a time get position null, and until a part has finished its participants occupy its places (during Q2, riders eliminated in Q1 are ranked from 13th down). Formula 1 qualifying comes as a table of its own, with part null.

**Plans:** Every plan, Free included.

get.description:
A single search over teams (individual competitors included), players, managers, referees, leagues, fixtures, venues, racing series and races; each hit’s type names the endpoint family its id is valid for. Those families are /v2/teams, /v2/players, /v2/managers, /v2/referees, /v2/leagues, /v2/fixtures, /v2/series and /v2/races (venue ids are covered in the note). Player hits include the player’s current team; fixture hits include the teams, league, start time and status; venue hits include city, country and capacity.

**Note:** This API models every competitor as a team, so tennis players and other individual-sport athletes are returned with type team. type is a closed set — manager, referee, series and race were added on 2026-10-24, fixture and venue on 2026-11-04 — so ignore any value your client does not recognise. Three fields depend on the type and are null for all others: venue (a Venue), team (the player’s current team, as a TeamRef) and fixture ({ home, away, league, startTime, status }, with status as the coarse StatusType — the score and the rest come from /v2/fixtures/{id}). Venue hit ids work with /v2/venues/{id} and match the id in Fixture.venue and TeamDetail.venue. Since 2026-11-04 team hits include gender (male | female | mixed, matching TeamDetail), which lets you mark a women’s team without a call to /v2/teams/{id}; it is null for every other type. Venue hits come from a separate search at the source and are merged in by relevance. Passing type (since 2026-11-09) restricts the list to that type, returns 20 hits per page and reaches much further than the mixed list: ask for ?q=smith&type=player and pages go up to 50; hasNextPage stays true as long as a page is full. type=series comes from the mixed list and is therefore a single page — the source offers no paged search for series. Managers and referees also get image, a photo on our CDN (since 2026-11-04; null if the source has none); series, races, fixtures and venues always have image null.

get.description:
All markets the bookmaker offers on a fixture — result (1X2), double chance, draw no bet, winner, first to score, both teams to score, Asian handicap, handicap / point spread, goal / card / corner / points totals, the cricket toss winner, most sixes, a hundred / fifty in the match, and next goal (live). Each comes with opening and current prices in decimal and fractional form, the direction of the latest price change, its suspension state and, once the match is over, the winning selections. Available on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans.

**Note:** Every market has a key that stays the same for the whole fixture, built from the kind followed by :period, :line and :live ("result", "result:half1", "totalGoals:2.5", "asianHandicap:-1.25", "winner:live"); use it to merge WebSocket odds frames. During play the bookmaker shows the in-play market (live: true, key ending …:live) alongside the now-closed pre-match market, which keeps its final prices from before kick-off. line is the figure of a total or the handicap of the HOME side; when the line moves, the market gets a new key. decimal equals 1 + fractional, rounded to 2 decimal places. winning is null until settlement and wherever nobody settles the market, and settledBy tells you who set it. The source leaves some markets unsettled: on NBA games the point spread (handicap) and the first-quarter winner were still null hours after full time when we checked on 2026-11-05, and so were football Asian handicaps and total cards on every finished fixture days later (checked 2026-11-12), while results, winners and goal totals came within minutes (settledBy "source"). Since 2026-11-12 we settle two of those from the final result ourselves, marked settledBy "computed" and never overriding a flag the source has set: football Asian handicaps on half lines, from the regular-time score, and football total cards on half lines when the match saw yellow cards only, all shown to players on the pitch and with the incidents and statistics in agreement. Any other market the source leaves open stays null permanently. A bet is decided by the bookmaker’s own rules. An empty markets list, with updatedAt null, means the bookmaker offers nothing on the fixture — typical for minor leagues and matches far in the future. Over REST the data refreshes roughly every 30 seconds in play; subscribe to odds:{id} to receive every price change.

**Plans:** Requires Pro, Business or Enterprise; a Free or Starter key receives 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

get.description:
The timeline of a basketball, ice hockey or darts match, oldest first, filled live about 5 seconds behind play since 2026-11-13 (Enterprise only): every shot and where it was taken (made or missed; on target, blocked or saved), goals with the scorer and assists, penalties and their length, faceoffs, hits, timeouts and the score of each period — and in darts each dart with the bed it landed in and each visit with its score, the points left to get, and the legs and sets.

**Note:** Events the source withdrew and clock housekeeping are left out. In basketball a made basket has type goal, with points set. Basketball and ice hockey positions run 0–100; home plays towards x = 100 and away towards x = 0 throughout. The source does not say which way a team attacks (its ice hockey spots swap ends every period, and some basketball games swap baskets at half-time), so each side’s positions are mirrored for a period (x → 100 − x, y → 100 − y) whenever its shots in that period fall in the wrong half; a side without shots in a period takes its direction from the opponent and from the neighbouring periods — so while a match is live, an event from a period with no shots yet can still move once shots arrive (sent as an upsert frame). Darts: a dartThrow carries darts.score, number, multiplier, ring (single, double, treble, outerBull, bull or miss), bed (for a single, the inner or outer single bed as the source gives it, since 2026-11-13; null for every other ring) and doubleAttempt; a visit carries darts.score as the visit total, dartsThrown, remaining (what each side still needs), legs and sets; checkout is the visit that took a leg, with checkoutDouble; legWon has the legs in homeScore / awayScore, and setWon and matchWon close the set and the match. Darts events have no position, and some darts competitions are reported visit by visit only. While a match is in play the source can correct an event or take it back, so read the timeline again or follow tracking:{id}. Football and tennis have no timeline, so the list is empty for them.

post.description:
Kicks off an export of a single league season. JSON body: league (DataSportsAPI league id), season (taken from /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons) and format, one of json (the default — a single season.json containing league, season, rounds, all fixtures, standings, top players and top teams exactly as the endpoints return them), csv or parquet (each giving two flat tables: fixtures and standings). The response is 202 with the export object, in status pending.

**Note:** Fixtures are collected round by round, so a competition our data source does not split into rounds (NBA and NHL regular seasons) produces an export without fixtures; the export’s error field lists whatever could not be read (“not included: topPlayers”). Because we mirror the source’s listing, a match that was postponed and replayed later may appear twice — once as the postponed fixture and once as the played one, each with its own id (Premier League 25/26: 381 fixtures, one of them postponed). Columns in the CSV / Parquet files — fixtures: fixture_id, sport, start_time, round, round_name, status, status_description, home_team_id, home_team, away_team_id, away_team, home_score, away_score, winner, venue; standings: table, primary, position, team_id, team, played, wins, draws, losses, scores_for, scores_against, points, zone.

**Plans:** Requires Business or Enterprise; any lower plan receives 403 endpoint_not_in_plan.

bearerAuth.description: Your secret API key: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…`. Publishable widget keys (`dsa_pub_…`) work only for the endpoints widgets read, from the sites registered on them.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Your plan's request quota for the current period (UTC month on paid plans, UTC day on Free).

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests still available in the current period.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the period ends and the quota refills.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

Fixture.description: A single match. Every endpoint and every WebSocket snapshot returns it in this same shape.

sport.description: Slug of the sport, matching the values listed by /v2/sports.

startTime.description: Kick-off time. Holds the scheduled start until the source logs the actual kick-off, which then takes its place (the live feed delivers it a few minutes after play begins). Identical across all endpoints and WebSocket deltas.

league.description: Competition the fixture belongs to. It is null if the source places the fixture in a competition that has no matching league (observed in minor regional football, e.g. South Africa’s National Second Division on 2026-10-23); in that case season and round are null as well.

season.description: Season the fixture is part of.

round.description: Round of the fixture, for competitions organised in rounds.

home.description: The home team. Null until that slot is settled, e.g. while the source still shows a placeholder like "WQF1" (winner of quarter-final 1).

away.description: The away team. Null until that slot is settled (for instance a "WQF1" placeholder from the source).

winner.description: Stays null until status.type is finished, and also when a fight ends as a no contest (`fightResult.method` noContest). When penalties decide the match, this is always the shoot-out winner regardless of the source (which, on a second leg, reports the team that won the 90 minutes). If the source omits the winner, or declares a draw in a sport where draws are impossible (finishes in regular time or overtime; cricket excluded), we derive it from the score.

venue.description: Where the match is played, if known (frequently null in lower divisions). Populated on /fixtures/{id}, and in date lists when the source provides it. Round, team, player and live lists never include a venue, so a null there means "omitted" rather than "unknown" — fetch /fixtures/{id} to get it.

clock.description: The match clock. Null if the source keeps no clock for this fixture, and after the match ends.

firstToServe.description: Deprecated (2026-10-23); mirrors `serving`. Because the source refreshes it each game / leg, it reflects who is serving (throwing) at the moment, not who served first. Use `serving` instead.

serving.description: Tennis, darts and other sports with a serve: which side is currently serving (throwing), refreshed by the source every game / leg. Null if the source gives no indication.

servedFirst.description: Darts: which side threw the opening dart of the match (`serving` is whoever is throwing now). Fixed for the whole match once play begins; null before that, when the source does not say, and in every other sport (only darts data carries it). Since 2026-11-11.

homeSeed.description: For seeded events such as tennis draws or playoff brackets (basketball, …): the seed of the home side ("1", "12") or its entry status ("WC" wild card, "Q" qualifier, "LL" lucky loser, "PR" protected ranking, …), exactly as shown in the draw. Null for an unseeded side.

awaySeed.description: Seed or entry status of the away side; see homeSeed.

note.description: Cricket: the match note supplied by the source, which becomes the result line at the end ("Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 37 runs"). Intended for display only.

battingSide.description: Cricket: which side is currently at the crease. Null outside a live innings and in every other sport.

fightResult.description: MMA / boxing: how, in which round and at what time the fight ended. Null before status.type reaches finished, and when the source supplies no method.

fightDiscipline.description: Combat sports: the bout’s discipline, when the source labels it (the `mma` sport includes boxing, kickboxing and Muay Thai cards as well). Only some cards are labelled (ONE, Queensbury, certain OKTAGON fights; never UFC or PFL), so a null value does not imply MMA.

referee.description: Match official, if the source names one (football and a few other sports; in cricket, the match referee). Present on /fixtures/{id}; always null in lists, where it is omitted.

homeManager.description: Manager or head coach of the home side for this match, if the source names one. Present on /fixtures/{id}; null in lists.

awayManager.description: Manager or head coach of the away side; behaves like homeManager.

surface.description: Tennis: the surface the match is played on. Present on /fixtures/{id} and in live lists; null in other sports.

discipline.description: Tennis: whether it is singles or doubles. Present on every fixture endpoint, in lists and in WebSocket snapshots; null in other sports and when the source specifies neither. Since 2026-11-11.

toss.description: Cricket: the toss result, after it has taken place. Present on /fixtures/{id}; null in other sports.

umpires.description: Cricket: the on-field umpires, named as the source writes them (frequently with a country code, e.g. "Asif Yaqoob (PAK)"). Null when none are listed and in other sports.

tvUmpire.description: Cricket: the TV (third) umpire, formatted as for umpires.

previousLegFixtureId.description: Two-legged ties and playoff series: the DataSportsAPI id of the preceding leg / game, when the source links the two. Look that id up on /fixtures/{id} to get the first-leg score.

aggregateWinner.description: Once the return leg of a two-legged tie is over: the side that went through. Taken from the source’s verdict when available; otherwise from `aggregated` (the higher total advances) or, if the aggregate is level, from the shoot-out. Null in every other case, including a level aggregate the source leaves unresolved (an away-goals rule). Compare `winner`, which refers to this match alone: when a second leg goes to penalties both fields name the shoot-out winner, but otherwise they can disagree (a side may win the second leg yet be eliminated). Filled on /fixtures/{id}; in lists and live snapshots it can be null.

fightCard.description: MMA / boxing: the bout’s section of the card, its running order and its weight class, if the source lists them.

attendance.description: Crowd figure, if the source reports one (observed for NBA and MLB games, frequently only after the game has started). Present on /fixtures/{id}; omitted (null) in lists.

matchFormat.description: Darts and esports: the format of the match (best of N sets / legs / games), if the source states it. Null in other sports.

inningState.description: Baseball: the live game situation — inning, half, balls, strikes, outs and runners on base. Null when the game is not in progress or interrupted, and in other sports. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas.

timeouts.description: Basketball: timeouts each side has left. Null outside an in-progress or interrupted game, and whenever the source does not track them. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas.

downAndDistance.description: American football: the current down, distance and field position. Null when the game is not in progress or interrupted, and in other sports. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-09.

varCheck.description: Football: an ongoing VAR review. Null when no review is under way, outside play and in other sports. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-09.

bonus.description: Basketball: whether each side is in the bonus. Null outside an in-progress or interrupted game, and whenever the source does not report it. The source’s live feed never carries it, so it appears in REST responses and lists only. Available since 2026-11-09.

finalResultOnly.description: True if the source provides only the final result for this fixture, with no live score, clock or events during play (available since 2026-11-09).

durations.description: Sports played in sets or rounds: the length of every finished period (available since 2026-11-04). Null for sports the source does not time by period (football, basketball, …) and until the first period is over. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas.

lineupsAvailable.description: Becomes true when the source publishes lineups for the fixture, whether predicted or official (check `confirmed` on /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups to tell them apart), and false if they are withdrawn. We set it the moment the source’s live feed announces lineups, or when a lineup we fetch contains players. Null means we have no information yet (no announcement observed, nothing fetched). WebSocket deltas carry it live — on fixture:{id} from before kick-off, and on the list channels once play starts. Available since 2026-11-04.

lineupsConfirmed.description: Becomes true when the official lineups are released (matching `confirmed` on /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups); otherwise behaves like lineupsAvailable, with null meaning we have no information. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-04.

type.description: High-level state, computed from `phase` (mapping in the StatusPhase table).

code.description: The source’s raw status code (the data dictionary lists every value); `phase`, `period` and `finish` give you its meaning ready-made.

description.description: Human-readable English label taken from our status table (status codes in the data dictionary) and adapted to the sport, for example "Halftime", "2nd half", "After penalties", "After extra time" (football), "After extra innings" (baseball), "After overtime" (basketball, ice hockey, …), "1st innings" (cricket) or "Coverage canceled". For a code we do not recognise, the source’s own wording is passed through. Use it for display, never for branching logic.

period.description: Period currently being played, or the one just completed during a break. Null before the start and after the end.

finish.description: The way the result was reached. Only set when `type` is finished; null otherwise.

current.description: The headline score you would see on a scoreboard: goals, points, sets won (tennis / volleyball) or runs (cricket, baseball), counting extra time / overtime. Shoot-out goals are excluded and reported in `penalties` instead — except in ice hockey, where the shoot-out winner is given one extra goal (3-3 after overtime becomes 3-4). Before the start, and for fixtures whose coverage was canceled, it is null.

periods.description: The score split by period and keyed by PeriodKey — goals per half, quarter or period; games per set in tennis; points per set in volleyball and table tennis; runs per inning in baseball. Extra periods are included too: football and futsal use `extra1` / `extra2`; American football, basketball, handball, ice hockey, water polo and others use `overtime`; baseball extra innings run from `period10` upwards (`overtime` only if the source reports extra-innings runs as one total). When the source’s breakdown is complete the values sum to `current`; it is occasionally incomplete (some baseball leagues omit innings, a few futsal matches lack a half), and ice hockey decided by a shoot-out is intentionally one goal short (see `current`). Esports uses one key per game (map), with a title-dependent meaning: Counter-Strike stores 1 for each map a side won and 0 for the rest (maps not played count as 0, through period5 in a best of 3); in League of Legends it is the side’s kill count in game N, so the values do not sum to `current`, which counts games won. Each game’s winner and score are on /fixtures/{id}/games. Empty when the source gives no breakdown.

tieBreaks.description: Tennis: points won in each set’s tie-break, using the same keys as `periods` (e.g. { "period2": 7 }).

normalTime.description: Score when regulation time ended, if the source provides it.

penalties.description: Goals converted in a penalty shoot-out. In ice hockey the shoot-out winner gets 1 here and the loser 0, in line with the single goal added to `current`.

aggregated.description: Combined score across both legs of a two-legged tie.

series.description: Playoff series: number of games this side has won in the series to date (basketball, baseball, ice hockey, water polo).

point.description: Tennis: score within the current game — "0" | "15" | "30" | "40" | "A", or a plain number ("0"–"N") during a tie-break. Darts: the points the side still has to score in the current leg ("501" when a leg starts). Null when play is neither in progress nor interrupted.

redCards.description: Football: number of red cards this side has received, counting second yellows.

innings.description: Cricket: each innings of this side, keyed inning1…N. Empty in other sports.

hits.description: Baseball: hit total, i.e. the H in the R/H/E line.

errors.description: Baseball: error total, i.e. the E in the R/H/E line.

CricketInnings.description: A single cricket innings played by one side.

wickets.description: Number of wickets that have fallen.

overs.description: Overs delivered, in cricket notation (49.5 means 49 overs plus 5 balls).

targetRunRate.description: Run rate the chasing side needs to reach its target.

Clock.description: Timing data for a match. Running clocks (football, rugby, …): compute elapsed = periodOffsetSeconds + (now − periodStartedAt) and minute = floor(elapsed / 60) + 1; once periodEndSeconds is passed, display periodEndSeconds / 60 followed by "+" and the extra minutes. This applies only while status.phase is inprogress. Stop clocks (basketball, handball, ice hockey, …): playedSeconds is the value at playedAt and advances only while `running` is true. Tennis, table tennis, badminton and esports (set / map sports) carry only `periodStartedAt` (start of the current set or map), and only if the source sends it — the clock as a whole is frequently null. A field is null whenever the source does not provide it for that sport; the entire clock is null when no clock exists and after the match ends. Lists other than /fixtures/{id} may include fewer clock fields (static values such as periodLengthSeconds can be null there).

periodStartedAt.description: Moment the clock for the current period was started.

periodOffsetSeconds.description: Running clock: seconds already on the clock at the start of the period (2700 for the second half in football). Unit: seconds.

periodEndSeconds.description: Running clock: clock reading, in seconds, at which regulation time for the period runs out (2700 for the first half in football). Unit: seconds.

maxExtraSeconds.description: Running clock: upper bound on the added time the source’s display permits after periodEndSeconds. Unit: seconds.

injuryTimeMinutes.description: Stoppage time announced for the current period. Unit: minutes.

playedSeconds.description: Stop clock: time played in seconds, valid at `playedAt`. Unit: seconds.

running.description: Stop clock: true while the game clock is ticking.

runningUpdatedAt.description: Time of the most recent change to `running`.

periodLengthSeconds.description: Stop clock: duration of a single regulation period. Unit: seconds.

overtimeLengthSeconds.description: Duration of a single overtime period. Unit: seconds.

periodCount.description: How many regulation periods the match has (in combat sports, the scheduled rounds).

lastPeriodEndedAt.description: End time of the latest completed period. During a break (half-time, between periods) this marks when the break started, so the break has lasted now − lastPeriodEndedAt. Used with football-style running clocks; null if the source sends nothing (before the first break, in other sports, or for data stored before 2026-11-04). Available since 2026-11-04.

FightResult.description: MMA / boxing: the way a completed fight was settled.

round.description: Round in which the fight finished.

roundTimeSeconds.description: Elapsed time in that round when the fight was halted (KO, TKO, submission, disqualification, …), if the source records it. Null for every decision (unanimous, split, majority, technical, drawn ones too): nothing stopped the fight, and the source’s figure cannot be trusted there. Unit: seconds.

Referee.description: The match official (for cricket, the match referee) and the career totals the source records for them. For a per-match rate, divide a total by `games`.

name.description: Name of the referee.

country.description: Country of the referee, if the source supplies it.

games.description: Number of matches the source has logged with this referee in charge, across the whole career and all competitions.

yellowCards.description: Yellow cards issued across those matches. Null in sports that have no cards (cricket).

redCards.description: Direct red cards issued across those matches. Null in sports that have no cards.

yellowRedCards.description: Dismissals for a second yellow across those matches. Null in sports that have no cards.

image.description: Referee photo hosted on our CDN. Null if no image exists or it has not been uploaded yet. Available since 2026-11-04.

Surface.description: Tennis: the type of court used for the match.

indoor.description: True for an indoor court and false for an outdoor one; null if the source does not specify.

name.description: Surface label as worded by the source, such as "Hardcourt outdoor". For display only.

CricketToss.description: Cricket: outcome of the coin toss.

winner.description: Toss winner; null if the team the source names matches neither participant.

decision.description: The choice the toss winner made.

FightCard.description: MMA / boxing: a bout’s placement on the event card.

section.description: The part of the card (main card, prelims, …), if the source specifies it.

order.description: Position of the bout in the source’s numbering of the card; larger numbers come later, and the main event carries the largest.

weightClass.description: Weight class of the bout, using the source’s naming ("light", "bantam", "feather", …).

FixturePatch.description: Contents of `changes` in a WebSocket delta: a partial Fixture that keeps the same field names and nesting. Deep-merge it into your local Fixture — nested objects merge key by key, while any other value (null included) overwrites. No fields beyond those listed here are ever sent.

status.description: Status fields that were modified. A status change always repeats type, phase and finish, plus period when it is known.

startTime.description: Updated start time, either because the fixture was rescheduled or because the source has logged the actual kick-off (see Fixture.startTime).

winner.description: Sent once the match is over.

homeScore.description: Modified fields of the home ScoreSide.

awayScore.description: Modified fields of the away ScoreSide.

clock.description: Since 2026-11-14 the whole Clock (every field, null where there is no value) is sent whenever any part of it changes. Deep-merging it gives the same result as before, and a client that held no clock now receives a complete one. A null value signals the match has ended; discard the clock.

firstToServe.description: Deprecated; carries the same value as `serving`.

servedFirst.description: Darts: which side opened the match, sent as soon as the source provides it. Since 2026-11-11.

battingSide.description: Cricket: side currently batting; null when nobody is.

inningState.description: Baseball: updated game state, always delivered as a complete object; null once play has stopped.

timeouts.description: Basketball: timeout counts that were modified; null once play has stopped.

downAndDistance.description: American football: fields that were modified (the full object when tracking begins); null once play has stopped. Available since 2026-11-09.

varCheck.description: Football: a full object when a VAR review begins, null when it finishes. Available since 2026-11-09.

durations.description: A newly finished period with its length in seconds (keyed as in ScoreSide.periods; null means the source removed it, so delete it), together with the updated total. Merge it the same way as a score map.

fightResult.description: MMA / boxing: how, in which round and when the fight finished, sent as a whole object once the source has it. Expect it in a delta after the one that ends the fight, since the source releases it ~20–60 s after the winner is known.

lineupsAvailable.description: True when lineups are published and false when they are pulled, sent as soon as the source announces it, including before kick-off (fixture:{id}). Available since 2026-11-04.

lineupsConfirmed.description: Signals that the official lineups have been released. Available since 2026-11-04.

ScoreSidePatch.description: Only the ScoreSide fields that changed.

current.description: The headline score you would see on a scoreboard: goals, points, sets won (tennis / volleyball) or runs (cricket, baseball), counting extra time / overtime. Shoot-out goals are excluded and reported in `penalties` instead — except in ice hockey, where the shoot-out winner is given one extra goal (3-3 after overtime becomes 3-4). Before the start, and for fixtures whose coverage was canceled, it is null.

normalTime.description: Score when regulation time ended, if the source provides it.

penalties.description: Goals converted in a penalty shoot-out. In ice hockey the shoot-out winner gets 1 here and the loser 0, in line with the single goal added to `current`.

aggregated.description: Combined score across both legs of a two-legged tie.

series.description: Playoff series: number of games this side has won in the series to date (basketball, baseball, ice hockey, water polo).

point.description: Tennis: score within the current game — "0" | "15" | "30" | "40" | "A", or a plain number ("0"–"N") during a tie-break. Darts: the points the side still has to score in the current leg ("501" when a leg starts). Null when play is neither in progress nor interrupted.

redCards.description: Football: number of red cards this side has received, counting second yellows.

hits.description: Baseball: hit total, i.e. the H in the R/H/E line.

errors.description: Baseball: error total, i.e. the E in the R/H/E line.

periods.description: Just the periods whose value changed. A null value means the source removed that period, so delete it.

tieBreaks.description: Just the tie-breaks whose value changed; null means one was removed.

innings.description: Just the innings that changed. Merge them key by key, as with periods; any innings left out keeps its previous value.

TeamRef.description: Compact team reference embedded in other objects (fixtures, standings, players, leaders).

name.description: Name of the team. Individual sports (tennis, table tennis, darts, MMA, …) also model each competitor as a team — a single player, or a doubles pair.

shortName.description: Abbreviated display name, if the source provides one.

code.description: Abbreviation of 1–4 characters as used on scoreboards (e.g. "ARS", "LA"); generated artificially for individual sports.

image.description: Team logo hosted on our CDN; null if the team has no image.

name.description: Name of the team. Individual sports (tennis, table tennis, darts, MMA, …) also model each competitor as a team — a single player, or a doubles pair.

shortName.description: Abbreviated display name, if the source provides one.

code.description: Abbreviation of 1–4 characters as used on scoreboards (e.g. "ARS", "LA"); generated artificially for individual sports.

image.description: Team logo hosted on our CDN; null if the team has no image.

country.description: Country the team is based in or represents.

colors.description: Kit colours in #rrggbb form. Null when the source has no real colours for the team (the source fills in a placeholder blue for every individual competitor and most minor teams).

gender.description: Whether the team is men’s, women’s or mixed; null if the source does not specify.

national.description: True for a national team, false for a club; null if the source does not specify.

kind.description: Distinguishes a team, a single competitor in an individual sport and a doubles pair; null if the source does not specify.

manager.description: Current manager or head coach, if the source names one.

person.description: For individual competitors the source profiles (tennis, MMA): date of birth, height, weight and so on. Null for everyone else.

record.description: MMA / boxing fighters: career win-draw-loss record together with how their most recent fights ended. Null for all other teams.

foundedOn.description: Founding date of the club, if the source has it (roughly half of the teams we have read); null otherwise. Available since 2026-11-09.

Person.description: Personal details of an individual competitor (`kind: individual`) for whom the source keeps a profile (tennis players, MMA fighters). Field names and units match Player.

weightKg.description: Body weight in kilograms (for MMA, the weight the fighter is listed at).

reachCm.description: Arm reach, for MMA. Unit: cm.

nickname.description: MMA ring name or nickname, such as "Storm".

weightClass.description: Weight class in the source’s wording (MMA: "feather", "light", "bantam", …).

birthplace.description: Place of birth in the source’s wording ("San Candido, Italy").

residence.description: Place of residence in the source’s wording ("Monte Carlo, Monaco").

handedness.description: Tennis: which hand the player plays with.

turnedPro.description: Tennis: year the player became a professional.

prizeMoneySeason.description: Tennis: prize money earned in the current season.

prizeMoneyCareer.description: Tennis: total prize money earned over the career.

LeagueRef.description: A league or competition. /v2/leagues/{id} and every league list return this same shape.

name.description: Name of the league or competition.

sport.description: Slug of the sport, matching the values listed by /v2/sports.

category.description: How the source groups the league: by country ("England"), region ("International", "North America", "World"), tour ("ATP", "WTA") or game (esports: "Counter Strike"). It is not necessarily a country; use `country` for that.

country.description: Country of the league when its category is a country; null for regions, tours and games.

image.description: League logo hosted on our CDN; null if the league has no image.

priority.description: The source’s prominence ranking for the competition, handy for ordering leagues: a higher value means a bigger competition (for example 719 for the Champions League, 704 for the Premier League, 702 for LaLiga, 519 for Primeira Liga), and 0 means unranked. It is filled only where the source supplies it: on the league embedded in a fixture and in the /v2/fixtures?date&sport day lists. Everywhere else — league profiles, directories, search — it is null, as it is on rows saved before 2026-11-04. Available since 2026-11-04.

code.description: Two-letter code supplied by the source. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, apart from XK for Kosovo and four codes for the UK home nations (England EN, Scotland SX, Wales WA, Northern Ireland NX). Null if unknown.

name.description: Country name in English.

flag.description: Flag image (PNG) hosted on our CDN. Null when there is no code or the image has not been uploaded yet. Available since 2026-11-04.

name.description: Full season name, such as "Premier League 26/27".

year.description: Display label in the source’s format: "26/27" or "2026/2027" when the season spans two years, "2026" for a calendar-year season. Use startYear / endYear for sorting and filtering.

startYear.description: Year in which the season begins (2026 for both "26/27" and "2026"); null if the label cannot be parsed.

endYear.description: Year in which the season finishes (2027 for "26/27"; equal to startYear for a calendar-year season); null if the label cannot be parsed.

Round.description: One round within a league season.

number.description: Round number from the source. Treat it as an opaque key rather than a sequence: cups count rounds by how many entrants remain (32 for a tennis "Round of 64"), and playoff rounds get large values (636). Use it with /v2/leagues/{id}/fixtures.
