fightCard.description: MMA and boxing: the bout’s card section, position on the card and weight class, if our data source lists them.

attendance.description: Crowd size, if our data source reports one (observed for NBA and MLB games, often appearing only after the game has started). Populated on /fixtures/{id}; lists return null because it is not included.

matchFormat.description: Match format for darts and esports — best of N sets / legs / games — when our data source provides it. Other sports get null.

inningState.description: Baseball only: the game situation right now — inning, half, balls, strikes, outs and runners on base. It is null while the game is not in progress or interrupted, and in every other sport. WebSocket deltas carry it live.

timeouts.description: Basketball: timeouts left for each side, filled only during an in-progress or interrupted game and only if our data source tracks them; null otherwise. WebSocket deltas carry live updates.

downAndDistance.description: American football only: down, distance and field position at this moment. It is null while the game is not in progress or interrupted, and in every other sport. Delivered live through WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-09.

varCheck.description: Football only: an ongoing VAR review; null when there is none, outside play, and for every other sport. Delivered live through WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-09.

bonus.description: Basketball only: the side or sides in the bonus. It is null while the game is not in progress or interrupted, and when our data source gives no value; the source’s live feed lacks it, so you only get it over REST and in lists. Available since 2026-11-09.

finalResultOnly.description: `true` if our data source covers only the final result of this fixture, with no live score, clock or events during play (since 2026-11-09).

durations.description: Sports played in sets or rounds: the length of every finished period (since 2026-11-04). Null for sports our data source does not time by period (football, basketball, …) and until the first period is over. Delivered live through WebSocket deltas.

lineupsAvailable.description: `true` once our data source has published lineups for the fixture, whether predicted or official (`confirmed` on /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups tells you which); `false` if they were withdrawn. We set it the moment the source’s live feed announces lineups, or when a lineup we fetch contains players. Null means we have no information (no announcement observed, nothing fetched). WebSocket deltas carry it live — on fixture:{id} from before kick-off, and on the list channels once play starts. Available since 2026-11-04.

lineupsConfirmed.description: `true` once official lineups have been released (`confirmed` on /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups), set in the same way as lineupsAvailable; null means we have no information. Delivered live through WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-04.

playerMatch.description: The player’s own involvement in this fixture, or null when our data source has nothing listed.

PlayerMatch.description: One player’s personal involvement in a single fixture.

onBench.description: `true` if the player was a named substitute who never came on.

rating.description: Player’s match rating (for example 7.4), rounded to two decimal places; null if there is none — the player did not take part, was not rated, or the match has not been played yet.

statistics.description: Statistics for this match as supplied with the player’s fixture list, using the same keys as lineup statistics (football: minutesPlayed; basketball: points, rebounds, assists, fieldGoalsMade, fieldGoalsAttempted, secondsPlayed, plusMinus …; ice hockey: goals, assists, shotsOnGoal, secondsPlayed …). All …Percentage values are on a 0–100 scale. An empty object when nothing is available.

incidents.description: Per-player tallies built from the match incidents, e.g. goals (penalties included), penaltyGoals (spot-kicks among those goals), assists, yellowCards, redCards …; an empty object if nothing applies.

RankingTypeInfo.description: An entry in GET /v2/rankings describing one ranking table; use its `type` with GET /v2/rankings/{type}.

type.description: Identifier of an available ranking table; GET /v2/rankings lists them all with names.

name.description: Human-readable name, such as "ATP singles ranking".

gender.description: Whether the ranking is for men or women; null for rankings of countries.

entry.description: What each row of the ranking represents.

Ranking.description: A full ranking table, as returned by GET /v2/rankings/{type}.

type.description: Identifier of an available ranking table; GET /v2/rankings lists them all with names.

updatedAt.description: Time of our data source’s most recent update to the table.

RankingRow.description: A single entry in a ranking table.

position.description: Rank, where 1 is the top spot. In MMA division rankings the champion leads the list with position 0.

previousPosition.description: Rank in the ranking’s previous edition (0 marks the MMA champion); null if our data source does not provide it.

points.description: Points in the ranking. UEFA uses coefficients and UTR the rating itself (e.g. 16.45); rankings with no points, such as MMA, give null.

previousPoints.description: Previous edition’s points; null if our data source does not include them.

bestPosition.description: Highest rank ever reached (tennis); null for other rankings.

tournamentsPlayed.description: Number of tournaments that count towards the total (ATP); null for other rankings.

team.description: Team-type object for whoever is ranked; tennis players and fighters are modelled as teams too. In a ranking of countries this is null.

league.description: For a country ranking (UEFA): that country’s top league; null for other rankings.

country.description: Country of the team or competitor, or — for UEFA’s country ranking — the ranked country itself; null if unknown.

Category.description: A bucket of leagues inside a sport, forming the top tier of the league directory.

id.description: Category identifier. Use it as the `category` parameter of GET /v2/leagues, or of GET /v2/fixtures to list that category’s fixtures on a given day (since 2026-11-04).

name.description: Category label: a country such as "England", a region such as "International" or "World", a tour such as "ATP", or a game in esports.

country.description: The country this category represents, if it is a country; null for regions, tours and games. Pass its `code` to GET /v2/leagues as `country`.

PlayerStatisticsRow.description: A single player’s row in the player-statistics explorer for a league season.

player.description: The player, in the reference shape used by every other object.

team.description: Club the player represented in this league season — after a mid-season move, the most recent one.

statistics.description: Totals for the season in the requested statistics group, keyed with v2 season-statistic names (identical to /v2/players/{id}/statistics: averageRating, goals, expectedGoals, shotsOnGoal, cleanSheets, …; `…Percentage` runs 0–100). Keys our data source omits for a player are left out, and averageRating is missing for unrated players (for whom the source sends 0).

SeriesRef.description: A racing series, which plays the role of a league in race sports: a motorsport championship, or in cycling the complete men’s or women’s road calendar. Races sit inside its seasons, and /v2/series/{id}/standings ranks competitors across a season.

name.description: Name of the series, for example "Formula 1", "MotoGP" or "NASCAR Cup Series". Cycling is organised differently: our data source bundles each gender’s road races into a single series ("Cycling Men", "Cycling Women").

Circuit.description: The track hosting a motorsport race.

name.description: Name of the track ("Circuit of the Americas").

city.description: City where the circuit is located.

country.description: Country where the circuit is located.

lengthMeters.description: Length of one lap, in metres. Unit: meters.

Race.description: Covers either a motorsport weekend (with practice, qualifying, sprint and race sessions) or a cycling event — a one-day race or a stage race.

name.description: What the race is called, e.g. "USA GP", "Tour de France", "Gran Piemonte".

season.description: Which season of the series the race falls in ("Formula 1 2026"); its id is what the /v2/series/{id}/… endpoints expect.

round.description: Championship round number as assigned by our data source; cancelled races may leave gaps in the sequence.

status.description: State of the race: notstarted before its first session, inprogress, finished after all sessions are complete, canceled, or postponed.

startDate.description: First day of the race (UTC); the sessions carry exact times. /v2/races and /v2/races/{id} never put it later than the first session’s day, while the race list of a season (/v2/series/{id}/races) keeps our data source’s dates.

endDate.description: Last day of the race (UTC). /v2/races and /v2/races/{id} never put it earlier than the last session’s day.

laps.description: How many laps the main race is scheduled for (motorsport).

distanceMeters.description: Main-race distance for motorsport, given in metres. Unit: meters.

category.description: Cycling: the race category (e.g. "World Tour 1 Grand Tour"), as our data source labels it.

winner.description: Who won — the main race in motorsport, the general classification in a cycling stage race — filled only after the finish. Drivers and riders are TeamRefs (kind individual), just as tennis players are.

sessions.description: All sessions, sorted by start time (oldest first).

RaceSnapshot.description: Snapshot sent on the race:{id} channel: the race, its sessions and the results of the current session.

race.description: Covers either a motorsport weekend (with practice, qualifying, sprint and race sessions) or a cycling event — a one-day race or a stage race.

session.description: Which session the results belong to — the live one if any, otherwise the most recently finished; null until a session has run.

results.description: Classification for that session, as from /v2/races/{id}/results?session=; [] while none exists.

RaceSummary.description: A race in a season listing, without sessions (fetch /v2/races/{id} for those).

name.description: What the race is called, e.g. "USA GP", "Tour de France", "Gran Piemonte".

season.description: Which season of the series the race falls in ("Formula 1 2026"); its id is what the /v2/series/{id}/… endpoints expect.

round.description: Championship round number as assigned by our data source; cancelled races may leave gaps in the sequence.

status.description: State of the race: notstarted before its first session, inprogress, finished after all sessions are complete, canceled, or postponed.

startDate.description: First day of the race (UTC); the sessions carry exact times. /v2/races and /v2/races/{id} never put it later than the first session’s day, while the race list of a season (/v2/series/{id}/races) keeps our data source’s dates.

endDate.description: Last day of the race (UTC). /v2/races and /v2/races/{id} never put it earlier than the last session’s day.

laps.description: How many laps the main race is scheduled for (motorsport).

distanceMeters.description: Main-race distance for motorsport, given in metres. Unit: meters.

category.description: Cycling: the race category (e.g. "World Tour 1 Grand Tour"), as our data source labels it.

winner.description: Who won — the main race in motorsport, the general classification in a cycling stage race — filled only after the finish. Drivers and riders are TeamRefs (kind individual), just as tennis players are.

RaceSession.description: A timed segment of a race. In motorsport that is a practice, qualifying, sprint or the race itself; in cycling it is a stage of a stage race (a one-day race consists of a single session, the race).

id.description: Identifier of the session, accepted by /v2/races/{id}/results?session=.

name.description: Name of the session as provided by our data source ("Practice 1", "Qualification", "Grand Prix", "Stage 5").

status.description: State of the session, using the fixture status types; null if our data source gives none.

lapsCompleted.description: Laps actually completed; fewer than `laps` if the race was shortened.

distanceMeters.description: How far the session covers in metres — for cycling, the stage length. Unit: meters.

weather.description: Weather conditions, available after the session has run.

trackCondition.description: Whether the track was dry or wet.

airTemperatureC.description: Measured air temperature, in degrees Celsius. Unit: celsius.

trackTemperatureC.description: Measured track-surface temperature in degrees Celsius (motorsport). Unit: celsius.

humidityPercent.description: Humidity as a relative percentage (0–100). Unit: percent.

safetyCar.description: `true` if the safety car was deployed; null if this was not reported.

winner.description: Winner of the session (the quickest in practice / qualifying), set only after the session ends.

parts.description: For knock-out qualifying and sprint qualifying sessions, the individual segments (Q1, Q2…) in run order. Every other session — and any where our data source lists none — has an empty array.

RaceSessionPart.description: One segment (MotoGP Q1 / Q2, Formula 1 Q1–Q3) of a knock-out qualifying session; segments are listed in run order.

id.description: Id of the segment; use it as session= on /v2/races/{id}/results to fetch only that segment’s results.

name.description: Label in the series’ own convention, numbered by run order: "Q1", "Q2", "Q3" in qualifying, "SQ1"… in sprint qualifying.

status.description: State of the segment; null when our data source gives none (Formula 1 segments).

startTime.description: Planned start time in UTC; null if our data source gives none.

RaceResult.description: A single competitor’s entry in the classification of a session or race.

position.description: Finishing position; null for a competitor who is not classified (check `state`).

competitor.description: Who raced: a driver or rider, represented as a TeamRef with kind individual.

team.description: Constructor or cycling team the competitor belongs to.

state.description: Whether the competitor is classified, and if not, the reason.

outReason.description: Reason for being out, in our data source’s wording ("Retired"); null for classified competitors.

carNumber.description: Race number on the car or bike (motorsport).

gridPosition.description: Grid slot at the start (races); null for a pit-lane start or when unknown.

startedFromPitLane.description: Set to `true` for a pit-lane start.

laps.description: Lap count according to our data source.

lapsBehind.description: How many laps down on the winner (for lapped cars); null if on the lead lap.

lapsLed.description: Number of laps spent in the lead.

timeMs.description: Overall time in ms for a race or stage, or the best lap in practice and qualifying. Null for lapped and non-classified competitors, and for a classified rider without a time in our data source. Unit: milliseconds.

gapMs.description: Gap to the winner. Null for the winner itself, for lapped or non-classified competitors, and for a classified rider with no time logged by our data source. Unit: milliseconds.

intervalMs.description: Gap to the competitor immediately in front; null for the winner, for lapped and non-classified competitors, and for a classified rider without a time in our data source. Unit: milliseconds.

bestLapMs.description: Quickest lap this competitor set, in ms (races). Unit: milliseconds.

bestLapNumber.description: Number of the lap on which that best time came.

fastestLap.description: `true` if this was the quickest lap of the whole session.

points.description: Championship points earned from this result.

tyreStints.description: Sequence of tyre stints (Formula 1 races only; empty elsewhere).

currentTyre.description: The set of tyres currently fitted (Formula 1 sessions while running, then the final set once over); null if our data source does not report it. Available since 2026-11-09.

inPit.description: Whether the car is currently in the pit lane during a live session (`true`); null if our data source does not report it. Available since 2026-11-09.

cycling.description: Secondary classifications, present on the overall result of a cycling stage race; null elsewhere.

part.description: When the classification is stitched together from qualifying segments (MotoGP qualifying, for which our data source has no combined table), the segment this entry was taken from ("Q2", "Q1"); timeMs / gapMs / intervalMs then refer to that segment. Null otherwise.

TyreStint.description: A run on a single set of tyres.

laps.description: Number of laps completed on this set.

CyclingStanding.description: Secondary-classification standings for one rider within a stage race’s overall result.

jersey.description: Leader’s jersey worn by this rider, if there is one.

pointsPosition.description: Where the rider sits in the points classification.

points.description: Points tallied in the points classification.

mountainsPosition.description: Where the rider sits in the mountains classification.

mountainsPoints.description: Points tallied in the mountains classification.

youngRiderPosition.description: Where the rider sits in the young-rider classification.

youngRiderTimeMs.description: Time on which the young-rider classification is based (total, in ms). Unit: milliseconds.

SeriesStandingsRow.description: A single entry in a series championship table.

position.description: Position in the championship.

competitor.description: The ranked entity — a driver or rider with `type=competitors`, a team with `type=teams`.

team.description: For drivers and riders, the team they race for; null in the teams table.

racesWithPoints.description: Number of races finished in the points.

WinProbability.description: DataSportsAPI’s in-house in-play win-probability model for football fixtures (explained in the docs). Its starting point is pre-match expected goals — which v2 builds from each team’s recent results in every competition, its domestic table and our league-strength coefficients, then mixes with the competition’s own table and form — and then adjusts for time remaining, score, red cards and momentum. It is an analytical indicator, not betting advice, and uses no bookmaker odds.

model.description: Version of the model, each described in the docs; new versions are announced in the changelog.

updatedAt.description: Time at which this estimate was calculated.

prematch.description: The estimate made before kick-off, with the inputs it was built from. Once computed it is fixed; later table updates do not touch it.

current.description: Most recent estimate — equal to the pre-match figure before kick-off and to certainty (1 / 0 / 0) once the match is over.

series.description: The probability curve, sorted oldest first by `at`. Points come at kick-off, at every match minute, and straight after each goal or red card, each start or end of a period and each big missed chance; before kick-off it is empty. Each point becomes permanent at two minutes old (or when the match ends) and is never edited after that, which keeps the curve faithful to what the model said in the moment. Passing `?since=` returns only the points after that instant.

inputs.description: Live inputs that the in-play estimate drew on.

WinProbabilityPrematch.description: The estimate made before kick-off, with the inputs it was built from. Once computed it is fixed; later table updates do not touch it.

home.description: Likelihood of a home win before kick-off, from 0 to 1. Unit: ratio.

draw.description: Likelihood of a draw before kick-off, from 0 to 1. Unit: ratio.

away.description: Likelihood of an away win before kick-off, from 0 to 1. Unit: ratio.

homeExpectedGoals.description: Expected goals the model assigns to the home side for the full match (λ home).

awayExpectedGoals.description: Expected goals the model assigns to the away side for the full match (λ away).

standings.description: `true` if the league table (attack / defence ratings) could be used; `false` means league or global averages stood in.

form.description: `true` if a pre-match form guide could be used.

allCompetitions.description: Model v2 only: `true` if the teams’ recent matches across all competitions could be used (strength derived from as many as their last 20 results, weighted by how old each is and by opponent strength). Null for model v1.

domesticTables.description: Model v2 only: `true` if the teams’ domestic league tables could be used (in a cup or European tie, each side’s own league table, made comparable with our league-strength coefficients). Model v1 leaves it null.

WinProbabilityState.description: A snapshot of the predicted outcome: home / draw / away probabilities at a given point in the match.

home.description: Chance, from 0 to 1, that the home side finishes the match with more goals on the scoreboard. Unit: ratio.

draw.description: Chance, from 0 to 1, that the scoreboard is level at the end (a penalty shoot-out does not count). home + draw + away = 1. Unit: ratio.

away.description: Chance, from 0 to 1, that the away side finishes the match with more goals on the scoreboard. Unit: ratio.

minute.description: Minute of the match this estimate refers to, counted like incidents: a goal in the 23rd minute gives 23, and 45+2 becomes minute 45 with addedMinute 2. Before kick-off it is null. Unit: minutes.

addedMinute.description: How far into added time, in minutes; null outside added time. Unit: minutes.

homeScore.description: Goals the home side had at that point. Null before kick-off.

awayScore.description: Goals the away side had at that point. Null before kick-off.

at.description: The UTC instant the estimate is tied to. On a curve point it marks the match moment the point stands for — the close of that minute, or the goal or whistle itself — read from the running match clock or, when the clock is stopped, estimated from kick-off, allowing 15 minutes for half-time. On `current` it is when the estimate was computed (before kick-off and in play) or when the match ended (once finished). Along the series it only ever goes up. Null only for points saved before 2026-10-22 without a known kick-off time.

WinProbabilityPoint.description: One point on the win-probability curve: the estimate together with the reason it was recorded.

home.description: Chance, from 0 to 1, that the home side finishes the match with more goals on the scoreboard. Unit: ratio.

draw.description: Chance, from 0 to 1, that the scoreboard is level at the end (a penalty shoot-out does not count). home + draw + away = 1. Unit: ratio.

away.description: Chance, from 0 to 1, that the away side finishes the match with more goals on the scoreboard. Unit: ratio.

minute.description: Minute of the match this estimate refers to, counted like incidents: a goal in the 23rd minute gives 23, and 45+2 becomes minute 45 with addedMinute 2. Before kick-off it is null. Unit: minutes.

addedMinute.description: How far into added time, in minutes; null outside added time. Unit: minutes.

homeScore.description: Goals the home side had at that point. Null before kick-off.

awayScore.description: Goals the away side had at that point. Null before kick-off.

at.description: The UTC instant the estimate is tied to. On a curve point it marks the match moment the point stands for — the close of that minute, or the goal or whistle itself — read from the running match clock or, when the clock is stopped, estimated from kick-off, allowing 15 minutes for half-time. On `current` it is when the estimate was computed (before kick-off and in play) or when the match ended (once finished). Along the series it only ever goes up. Null only for points saved before 2026-10-22 without a known kick-off time.

reason.description: What triggered this point on the curve.

Commentary.description: Automated match commentary for a football fixture, produced by DataSportsAPI AI using nothing but our own data. Goals, red cards, missed penalties, VAR decisions, the start and end of each period, big chances and lasting momentum shifts each get a short entry, and there are summaries at half-time and full time. Each entry is generated a single time and served identically to all clients.

entries.description: Entries ordered oldest first by `seq`, as in every timeline list. Empty until the first entry exists: commentary is only produced while someone is following the match (via this endpoint or the fixture:{id} channel; featured matches on datasportsapi.com always get it), so a match with no followers has none.

CommentaryEntry.description: A single entry of AI commentary.

seq.description: Sequence number within the fixture’s commentary — 1, 2, 3, … in writing order. A number is never reused.

kind.description: The subject of the entry; if it covers several events, the most significant one.

minute.description: Minute of the latest event the entry covers, counted as incidents are (45+2 is minute 45 with addedMinute 2). For summaries it is the whistle: 45 for halfTime, 90 for fullTime (120 after extra time); null on fullTime entries written before 2026-10-23. Unit: minutes.

addedMinute.description: How far into added time, in minutes; null outside added time. Unit: minutes.

text.description: Plain-text commentary of one or two English sentences (up to three for summaries), written by DataSportsAPI AI from our own match data alone (score, clock, events, statistics and our win-probability model). It contains no betting language.

model.description: Identifier of the generating model: "datasportsapi-ai" (DataSportsAPI AI). Entries served before 2026-11-02 carried the name of the underlying provider model instead.

PlayByPlay.description: Our data source’s play-by-play text, with an entry for each action (football, basketball, …). The source’s data provider writes it, not DataSportsAPI — see /commentary for our own AI commentary.

entries.description: Entries in chronological order, oldest first, as in every timeline list.

PlayByPlayEntry.description: A single play-by-play line from our data source’s text commentary.

type.description: The kind of action the entry describes.

side.description: Side that `player` belongs to (or the team the entry concerns); null for entries about the match as a whole (kick-off, period ends, delays).

period.description: Period in which the action took place; null when our data source gives none (football’s final whistle).

minute.description: Football: the match minute, with added time held separately (45+6 → minute 45, addedMinute 6). Null for clock sports (basketball uses `periodSecond`) and when our data source gives no time. Unit: minutes.

addedMinute.description: Added-time minutes in football (45+6 → 6); other cases give null. Unit: minutes.

periodSecond.description: Basketball and other clock sports: elapsed seconds in the current period. Football gives null. Unit: seconds.

periodSecondsLeft.description: Basketball and other clock sports: the game clock, counting down the seconds left in the period. Football gives null. Unit: seconds.

at.description: UTC time the action was logged, where our data source timestamps it (basketball); null elsewhere.

text.description: The English commentary text, verbatim from our data source.

player.description: The player the line concerns — the shooter, scorer, booked or fouling player, rebounder, and so on.

assist.description: Player credited with the assist, if our data source names one (basketball baskets).

goalkeeper.description: Goalkeeper our data source links to a shot (football). The source also fills it on a handful of basketball shots; what it means there has not been verified.

homeScore.description: scoreChange / penaltyScored: the home side’s score once the action is counted; null on all other entries.

awayScore.description: scoreChange / penaltyScored: the away side’s score once the action is counted; null on all other entries.

scoreType.description: scoreChange (basketball): how many points the basket counted for; null in football and on every other entry.

position.description: Basketball only: court location of the action, or null if our data source has none.

zone.description: Basketball: the area of the court; null when our data source provides none.

CourtPosition.description: Court location of a basketball action, expressed in our data source’s court units.

x.description: Position on the horizontal axis, measured in our data source’s court units.

y.description: Position on the vertical axis, measured in our data source’s court units.

LeagueDetail.description: Full league profile from /v2/leagues/{id}: everything in LeagueRef, plus the league’s level, current champion, record title-holders and the divisions directly above and below. Host countries are given per season (/v2/leagues/{id}/seasons/{seasonId}).

name.description: Name of the league or competition.

category.description: How our data source groups the league: by country ("England"), region ("International", "North America", "World"), tour ("ATP", "WTA") or game (esports: "Counter Strike"). It is not necessarily a country; use `country` for that.

country.description: Set when the league’s category is a country (that country); null for regions, tours and games.

image.description: CDN URL of the league logo; null if the league has none.

priority.description: Our data source’s prominence score for the competition, handy for sorting leagues: a higher value means a bigger competition (for example 719 for the Champions League, 704 for the Premier League, 702 for LaLiga, 519 for Primeira Liga), and 0 means unranked. It is filled only where the source supplies it: on the league embedded in a fixture and in the /v2/fixtures?date&sport day lists. Everywhere else — league profiles, directories, search — it is null, as it is on rows saved before 2026-11-04. Available since 2026-11-04.

tier.description: Tier within the national league pyramid: 1 for the top flight (Premier League), 2 for the second level (Championship); null for cups, international competitions and anything outside a pyramid.

gender.description: Whether the competition is for men or women; null if our data source does not specify.

titleHolder.description: Current title holder — the winner of the most recent completed season — if our data source names one.

titleHolderTitles.description: Total number of times the current title holder has won this competition.

mostTitles.description: Highest number of titles any single team has won.

mostTitlesTeams.description: Team or teams holding that record (more than one if tied); [] if our data source names none.

upperDivisions.description: Leagues directly above — the destination of promoted teams; [] for a top flight or a cup.

lowerDivisions.description: Leagues directly below — the destination of relegated teams; [] if none is listed.

currentSeasonStart.description: Start date of the current (or next) season, in UTC.

currentSeasonEnd.description: Planned end date of the current season, in UTC.

RefereeProfile.description: Referee profile from /v2/referees/{id}, with career totals across all competitions our data source covers (`games`, cards) and a breakdown per competition.

name.description: Full name of the referee.

country.description: Country of the referee, if our data source provides it.

games.description: Number of matches our data source has logged with this referee officiating, across the whole career and all competitions.

yellowCards.description: Bookings (yellow cards) handed out across those matches; null where the sport has no cards (cricket).

redCards.description: Straight red cards handed out across those matches; null where the sport has no cards.

yellowRedCards.description: Dismissals for a second yellow in those matches; null for sports that have no cards.

image.description: CDN URL of the referee’s photo; null if there is no image or it has not been uploaded yet. Available since 2026-11-04.

competitions.description: Per-competition breakdown of the career, ordered as our data source lists it; [] when there is none.

RefereeCompetition.description: Career numbers for a referee within a single competition; divide by `appearances` to get per-match rates.

appearances.description: Number of matches officiated in this competition.

yellowCards.description: Bookings (yellow cards) handed out in those matches.

ManagerProfile.description: Profile of a manager or head coach from /v2/managers/{id}, including the career record and the individual jobs that make it up.

id.description: The manager’s id — identical to the ManagerRef id on fixtures and teams.

name.description: Full name.

image.description: CDN URL of the manager’s photo; null if there is no image or it has not been uploaded yet. Available since 2026-11-04.

preferredFormation.description: Football: the formation they favour, in our data source’s notation ("4-2-3-1").

team.description: Team currently under their management; null if they are out of work.

career.description: Overall career results across all jobs our data source covers.

stints.description: Their positions, most recent first (as in transfer lists); [] if our data source has no history.

ManagerRecord.description: Results for a manager over a span of time — an entire career or a single job. Points per game is points / games.

draws.description: Matches drawn; null for sports with no draws.

scoresFor.description: Goals (or points, …) their teams scored; null if our data source does not provide them.

points.description: League points earned (in football, 3 per win and 1 per draw); null if our data source does not provide them.

ManagerStint.description: A single position held during a manager’s career.

team.description: Team they were in charge of.

to.description: Final day in charge (UTC). For their present job our data source supplies a FUTURE date — the contract end date it holds — rather than null.

record.description: Win / draw / loss record for that job; null when our data source has none (youth teams, older spells).

Trophy.description: An entry in a team’s trophy cabinet, representing one competition.

competitionType.description: Type of competition: national league, national cup or international.

major.description: `true` if our data source treats it as a major honour (a league or cup, as opposed to a super cup).

count.description: Number of times the team has won it.

seasons.description: Seasons in which it was won, most recent first (as in season lists). Can contain fewer items than `count` when our data source has no date for very old titles.

TrophySeason.description: A season in which a trophy was won. Our data source supplies only the label, not a season id.

year.description: Season label in our data source’s format ("23/24", "1932/1933", "2026").

startYear.description: Starting year of the season; null if the label cannot be parsed.

PositionHistoryPoint.description: A team’s league position as it stood at the close of a given week in the season.

week.description: Week number within the season, starting at 1 (following our data source’s weekly buckets).

to.description: Final day of the week, inclusive (UTC).

position.description: Where the team was placed in the league when the week ended.

fixtureIds.description: Fixture ids of the team’s matches in this competition during the week — typically one, and none in a blank week.

FighterCareerStatistics.description: Career statistics for an MMA fighter, calculated by our data source from the fights it holds detailed data on (which may not be the full career). Includes per-round and per-15-minute rates, 0–100 shares and time spent in each position. Keys take the match-statistics names (`significantStrikesHeadLanded`, `takedownsSucceeded`, …) and add the rate as a suffix. Null means the source has no figure.

strikesLandedPerRound.description: Average strikes landed per round, counting every strike.

strikesDistanceLandedPerRound.description: Average strikes landed per round while at distance.

strikesDistancePercentage.description: Strikes landed at distance as a share of all their landed strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

strikesClinchLandedPerRound.description: Average strikes landed per round from the clinch.

strikesClinchPercentage.description: Clinch strikes as a share of all their landed strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

strikesGroundLandedPerRound.description: Average strikes landed per round on the ground.

strikesGroundPercentage.description: Ground strikes as a share of all their landed strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

strikesReceivedPerRound.description: Average strikes taken from opponents per round.

significantStrikesLandedPerRound.description: Per-round average of significant strikes landed.

significantStrikesPercentage.description: Significant strikes as a share of all their landed strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

significantStrikesHeadLandedPerRound.description: Per-round average of significant strikes landed to the head.

significantStrikesHeadPercentage.description: Head strikes as a share of their significant strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

significantStrikesBodyLandedPerRound.description: Per-round average of significant strikes landed to the body.

significantStrikesBodyPercentage.description: Body strikes as a share of their significant strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

significantStrikesLegsLandedPerRound.description: Per-round average of significant strikes landed to the legs.

significantStrikesLegsPercentage.description: Leg strikes as a share of their significant strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

significantStrikesDistanceLandedPerRound.description: Per-round average of significant strikes landed at distance.

significantStrikesDistancePercentage.description: Significant strikes at distance as a share of all their significant strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

significantStrikesClinchLandedPerRound.description: Per-round average of significant strikes landed in the clinch.

significantStrikesClinchPercentage.description: Significant strikes in the clinch as a share of all their significant strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

significantStrikesGroundLandedPerRound.description: Per-round average of significant strikes landed on the ground.

significantStrikesGroundPercentage.description: Significant strikes on the ground as a share of all their significant strikes, 0–100. Unit: percent.

significantStrikesReceivedPerRound.description: Average significant strikes taken from opponents per round.

takedownsAttemptedPer15Min.description: Number of takedowns they attempt per 15 minutes.

takedownsSucceededPercentage.description: Share of their takedown attempts that succeed (landed / attempted), 0–100. Unit: percent.

takedownsReceivedPer15Min.description: Takedown attempts made against them per 15 minutes.

takedownsDefendedPer15Min.description: Of those attempts, the number they stopped per 15 minutes.

takedownsDefendedPercentage.description: Takedown defence rate — attempts stopped divided by attempts against them, 0–100. Unit: percent.

transitionsSucceededPer15Min.description: Ground advances (positional transitions) they completed per 15 minutes.

transitionsReceivedPer15Min.description: Positional transitions completed against them per 15 minutes.

submissionsAttemptedPer15Min.description: How many submissions they attempt per 15 minutes.

submissionsSucceededPer15Min.description: How many submissions they complete per 15 minutes.

submissionsSucceededPercentage.description: Submission success rate — completed divided by attempted, 0–100. Unit: percent.

submissionsReceivedPer15Min.description: How many submissions opponents attempt on them per 15 minutes.

submissionsDefendedPer15Min.description: Of those attempts, how many they fended off per 15 minutes.

submissionsDefendedPercentage.description: Share of submission attempts against them that they defend, 0–100. Unit: percent.

distanceSeconds.description: Total career time spent fighting at distance. Unit: seconds.

distanceSecondsPerRound.description: Average time per round spent at distance. Unit: seconds.

distancePercentage.description: Per-round average of the proportion of fight time spent at distance, 0–100. This is our data source’s own number: it can exceed 100 slightly (100.2 has been observed), and the distance, clinch and ground shares do not necessarily sum to 100. Unit: percent.

clinchSeconds.description: Total career time spent in the clinch. Unit: seconds.

clinchSecondsPerRound.description: Average time per round spent in the clinch. Unit: seconds.

clinchPercentage.description: Per-round average of the proportion of fight time spent in the clinch, 0–100 (caveats as for `distancePercentage`). Unit: percent.

clinchControlSeconds.description: Total career time spent controlling an opponent in the clinch. Unit: seconds.

clinchControlPercentage.description: Clinch control as a share of total fight time, 0–100. Unit: percent.

groundSeconds.description: Total career time spent on the ground. Unit: seconds.

groundSecondsPerRound.description: Average time per round spent on the ground. Unit: seconds.

groundPercentage.description: Per-round average of the proportion of fight time spent on the ground, 0–100 (caveats as for `distancePercentage`). Unit: percent.

groundControlSeconds.description: Total career time spent in control on the ground. Unit: seconds.

groundControlPercentage.description: Ground control as a share of total fight time, 0–100. Unit: percent.

FighterRecord.description: The CAREER record (e.g. 28-0-4) of a fighter in MMA or boxing. It is not the same as /v2/fixtures/{id}/form, where our data source gives pre-fight form inside the event’s competition (8-0-3 for that fighter, for example).

wins.description: Professional wins across all promotions, per our data source’s career record.

recent.description: The latest fights, at most five, each with its method, in chronological order. No career-wide breakdown by method is given, because our data source has none and only lists the recent fights it covers.

RecentFight.description: A recent fight as it appears in our data source’s record for the fighter.

result.description: Outcome for this fighter: win, draw, loss or no contest.

method.description: Finish method (KO, TKO, submission, decisions, …), or null when our data source does not record one.

TeamOfTheWeek.description: A line-up built from the highest-rated players of one round or week in a league season.

period.description: Round or week the team covers; null only when the list of periods could not be loaded.

formation.description: Formation of the line-up — "3-4-3" in football, "2-3" in basketball, for instance.

TeamOfTheWeekPeriod.description: A season round or week that has a team of the week attached.

id.description: Period identifier, used as the `period` parameter of /v2/leagues/{id}/team-of-the-week.

kind.description: Whether the period is a round or a span of days.

sequence.description: Position of the period within the season, starting at 1 (equal to the round number in round-based leagues).

round.description: For kind round: the round covered, as listed by /v2/leagues/{id}/rounds; null for other kinds.

roundName.description: For kind round: the round’s name in our data source’s wording; null for other kinds.

from.description: For kind week / month: when the span begins; null for a round.

to.description: Exclusive end of the span; null for a round.

publishedAt.description: Time our data source published this team of the week.

TeamOfTheWeekPlayer.description: An individual selected for a team of the week.

order.description: Slot in the line-up: 1 is the goalkeeper (football), then numbering runs from defence to attack following the formation.

player.description: The player, in the reference shape used by every other object.

team.description: Club they represented during the period.

position.description: Their position, as our data source’s code, interpreted per sport.

rating.description: Our data source’s match rating (0–10) that won them the spot.

fixtureId.description: Fixture id of the match the rating comes from.

PlayerAttributes.description: Attribute ratings for a football player across the years, together with their strengths and weaknesses, all from our data source’s own scouting model.

current.description: Latest ratings (yearsAgo 0); null if our data source does not rate the player at all.

history.description: All ratings our data source holds, starting with the current one (yearsAgo 0, 1, 2, …).

positionAverage.description: Average ratings for players in the same position, as a benchmark.

strengths.description: Strengths our data source attributes to the player, in the source’s order.

weaknesses.description: Weaknesses our data source attributes to the player.

positions.description: Detailed positions the player occupies, primary position first.

AttributeOverview.description: A set of attribute ratings on a 0–100 scale from our data source’s own model. Outfield players are rated on attacking / technical / tactical / defending / creativity, goalkeepers on saves / anticipation / ballDistribution / aerial / tactical; keys belonging to the other group are null.

yearsAgo.description: How many years back the rating is: 0 for now, 1 for the year before, etc.

position.description: Which position the ratings are given for — outfield and goalkeeper ratings come with different keys.

attacking.description: Outfield players’ attacking rating on a 0–100 scale; goalkeepers get null.

tactical.description: Tactical rating on a 0–100 scale, given to outfield players and goalkeepers alike.

saves.description: Goalkeepers’ saves rating on a 0–100 scale; outfield players get null.

VenueProfile.description: Profile of a stadium or arena covering its location, capacity, resident teams and match record for each sport.

id.description: The venue’s id — the same one found on Fixture.venue, TeamDetail.venue and venue search results.

name.description: Name of the stadium or arena.

city.description: City where the venue is located.

country.description: Country where the venue is located.

image.description: CDN URL of a venue photo; null if our data source has none or it has not been uploaded yet.

teams.description: Teams that use the venue as their home ground.

sports.description: One entry per sport played at the venue, busiest first; the sport slug is the `sport` value accepted by /v2/venues/{id}/fixtures.

VenueSportStatistics.description: Aggregate results for a single sport at a venue, across all matches our data source holds for it.

matchCount.description: Number of matches in that sport our data source records at the venue.

scored.description: Total goals (or points, runs …) scored by both sides in those matches.

homeWinPercentage.description: How often the home side won those matches, as a percentage (0–100). Unit: percent.

drawPercentage.description: How often those matches ended in a draw, as a percentage (0–100). Unit: percent.

NationalTeamRecord.description: A player’s international record for a single national side.

team.description: The national side, at senior or youth level.

appearances.description: Caps: international matches played for that side.

goals.description: Goals scored for that side in international matches.

debut.description: Date of their debut for the side; our data source gives only the day, so the time is midnight UTC.

SeasonHeatmap.description: A player’s areas of activity across a league season (football, covered leagues), built by summing their per-match heatmaps.

points.description: All points with their counts; draw them as a weighted density map.

fixtureCount.description: Number of matches feeding the heatmap, as counted by our data source.

fixtureIds.description: Fixture ids of those matches, to the extent our data source lists them.

SeasonHeatPoint.description: A single point on a season heatmap along with how many samples it holds.

x.description: Lengthwise position on the pitch, 0–100, using the match heatmap’s scale. Unit: percent.

y.description: Position across the width of the pitch, 0–100. Unit: percent.

count.description: Number of samples recorded at this point during the season; use it to weight the density.

PlayerRating.description: The rating a player received in a single match of a season, forming one point on their rating chart.

rating.description: Match rating from our data source (0–10).

side.description: Side they represented in that match.

PlayerCareerSeason.description: One row of a player’s career table: their statistics for a single competition, season and type.

season.description: Season of this row. Its id goes into the `season` parameter of /v2/players/{id}/statistics, together with this league.

team.description: Club they represented in this competition, or a national side in international competitions.

type.description: Which matches are included: overall, or regularSeason / playoffs in leagues that separate them.

statistics.description: Totals and averages for the season, keyed exactly as in /v2/players/{id}/statistics (naming conventions for season figures: `…PerMatch` is the total divided by matches, `…Per90` is per 90 minutes, `average…` is a season mean, `…Percentage` runs 0–100, and units are spelled out in the key). Ratings are rounded to two decimal places.

TeamRanking.description: One row from /v2/rankings/{type}, showing a team’s or competitor’s position in that ranking table.

type.description: Which ranking table this is; fetch the full table with GET /v2/rankings/{type}.

position.description: Current rank in the table (0 for MMA champions).

previousPosition.description: Rank in the previous edition; null if our data source does not provide it.

points.description: Ranking points — for UTR, the Universal Tennis Rating value itself (e.g. 16.45). Rankings without points return null.

bestPosition.description: Best rank ever reached (tennis), if our data source provides it.

bestPositionAt.description: Date the career-high rank was reached, if our data source provides it (which is rare).

tournamentsPlayed.description: Number of tournaments that count towards the total (ATP / WTA); null for other rankings.

PlayerOfTheSeason.description: Our data source’s player of the season for a completed league season — the highest average rating among players who met the playing-time threshold.

team.description: Team they played for that season.

rating.description: Average match rating across the season, from our data source, rounded to two decimal places.

appearances.description: Number of matches in which they received a rating.

PlayerOfTheSeasonCandidate.description: A candidate for player of the season; candidates are ordered by average rating, highest first.

team.description: Team they played for that season.

rating.description: Average match rating across the season, from our data source, rounded to two decimal places.

appearances.description: Number of matches in which they received a rating.

playedEnough.description: `true` if they have played enough of the season to be eligible.

Pitch.description: A single pitch in a baseball at-bat, or a play that happens between pitches, with its type, speed, location, outcome, the resulting count, runners and fielders.

kind.description: Whether this is a pitch or a play between pitches.

number.description: Pitch number within the at-bat, starting at 1; a play between pitches reuses the number of the preceding pitch (0 if no pitch has been thrown yet).

batterHand.description: Side of the plate the batter hits from.

pitchType.description: Kind of pitch; null for a play between pitches.

pitchName.description: Pitch name in our data source’s words ("Four-Seam Fastball"), intended for display only.

speedKmh.description: Speed of the ball at release. Unit: kilometersPerHour.

zone.description: Location where the ball crossed the plate, using MLB Statcast zones: 1–9 cover the strike zone as a 3 × 3 grid numbered from the top left from the catcher’s view, and 11–14 are the four quadrants outside it.

outcome.description: Result of the pitch; null for a play between pitches.

outcomeCode.description: Raw outcome code from our data source ("bB", "kKS", "oFO", …), for outcomes that `other` leaves unnamed.

endsAtBat.description: `true` if the at-bat finished on this pitch.

balls.description: Ball count once the pitch is recorded.

strikes.description: Strike count once the pitch is recorded.

outs.description: Outs in the half-inning once the pitch is recorded.

homeScore.description: Home side’s runs once the pitch is recorded.

awayScore.description: Away side’s runs once the pitch is recorded.

hit.description: `true` if the pitch resulted in a base hit.

wildPitch.description: `true` if it was a wild pitch.

passedBall.description: `true` if it was a passed ball.

overturned.description: `true` if the call was reversed after review.

battedBall.description: Details of the ball put in play, if any.

runners.description: Runner movements on the play in the order listed, including the batter once they start running.

fielders.description: Fielders who received credit on the play.

PitchRunner.description: Movement of one runner during a pitch or a play between pitches.

player.description: Someone named on a pitch as a runner or a fielder.

fromBase.description: Starting base: 0 for the batter at the plate, 1–3 for first through third base.

toBase.description: Base reached: 1–3 for first through third, 4 for home (a run scored); null if they were put out.

out.description: `true` if the runner was retired on the play.

PitchActor.description: Someone named on a pitch as a runner or a fielder.

id.description: The player’s id; null if our data source supplies none.

name.description: Name in our data source’s listing.

PitchFielder.description: Credit given to a fielder on a play.

player.description: Someone named on a pitch as a runner or a fielder.

role.description: The fielder’s part in the play.

order.description: Sequence within the play, where 1 is the first fielder to touch the ball.

BattedBall.description: Details of a ball hit into play.

hardness.description: Strength of contact off the bat.

Highlight.description: A match highlight video that lives on a third-party platform.

title.description: Video title, for example "Liverpool FC 0-1 Arsenal".

subtitle.description: Secondary title such as "Full Highlights", or the text of the post.

url.description: Link to the video on its platform (YouTube, X, …). DataSportsAPI does not host video, so link to or embed it from that platform.

thumbnailUrl.description: Thumbnail hosted by the video platform itself (i.ytimg.com, pbs.twimg.com); any other platform gives null.

main.description: `true` if our data source marks this as the match’s primary highlight.

countries.description: Two-letter codes of the countries to which our data source restricts the video (broadcast rights); an empty list means it is available everywhere.

publishedAt.description: Time our data source added the highlight.

Durations.description: Period lengths for sports played in sets or rounds (tennis, table tennis, badminton, volleyball, MMA, …), as timed by our data source.

periods.description: Duration in seconds of every COMPLETED period, using the same keys as ScoreSide.periods (in tennis period1 is the first set; in MMA / boxing the keys are the rounds). The period under way is excluded; its start is clock.periodStartedAt.

totalSeconds.description: Adds up `periods`: once the match has ended this is its playing time, not counting breaks between periods. Null when `periods` is empty. Unit: seconds.

SourceWinProbability.description: In-game win probability published by our data source itself for a fixture. Only available for American football (NFL), the single sport the source provides it for (verified 2026-11-04). Served over REST only — no WebSocket frame includes it. It is an analytical indicator, not betting advice.

model.description: Always "source", signalling that the estimate comes from the DATA SOURCE alongside its match data rather than from the football model we run ourselves, which lives at GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/win-probability (model values v1 to v3). Its methodology is unknown to us; no bookmaker odds are used on our side.

periodLengthMinutes.description: How long a regulation period lasts — 15 in the NFL. Unit: minutes.

periodCount.description: Number of regulation periods (4 in the NFL).

overtimeLengthMinutes.description: How long an overtime period lasts — 10 in the NFL regular season. Unit: minutes.

series.description: The probability curve, oldest point first, at about one point per minute of play (minutes can be missing, and the curve may start at 1). It grows as the game goes on; the last point is simply the source’s most recent estimate and need not be 0 or 1 when the game ends. Empty before kick-off and whenever the source has no data.

SourceWinProbabilityPoint.description: A single data point (one game minute) on the win-probability curve our data source publishes.

minute.description: Minute of game time the estimate applies to — measured in playing time rather than wall-clock time (an NFL quarter is 15 minutes, and overtime carries on the count: 61, 62, …). Unit: minutes.

home.description: Our data source’s estimated chance of a home win, from 0 to 1. Unit: ratio.

away.description: Our data source’s estimated chance of an away win, from 0 to 1 (equal to 1 − home, since the source does not model a tie). Unit: ratio.

FixtureCounts.description: Fixture totals for a UTC day, broken down by sport (today only) or by category within one sport (any day), A client can use it to print something like “1,172 matches today, 45 live” without walking through every page of the day.

date.description: Date (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) the counts refer to.

sport.description: Sport being counted; null covers all sports, in which case only today can be requested.

fixtureCount.description: All fixtures on the day regardless of state. With `sport`, this sums the per-category counts; without it, it sums the per-sport totals. For the same sport the two methods can disagree by a few percent, because the per-category list includes some matches carried over from late on the previous day.

liveCount.description: Fixtures currently live, taken from our live index (the same as /v2/sports); null unless `date` is today (UTC).

sports.description: When `sport` is omitted: each sport we cover that has fixtures today, ordered by fixture count, highest first. Empty when `sport` is given.

categories.description: With `sport` set: every category (country, region, tour) that has fixtures on the day, sorted by fixture count, highest first, then by name. Empty when `sport` is omitted, and for race sports (motorsport, cycling — use /v2/races).

SportFixtureCount.description: Today’s fixture total for a single sport, along with the number currently live.

fixtureCount.description: All fixtures on the UTC day regardless of state, taken from our data source’s per-sport daily counter.

liveCount.description: Fixtures currently live according to our live index — the same number /v2/sports and /v2/livescores report.

CategoryFixtureCount.description: How many fixtures one category (a country, region or tour) has on a given day.

category.description: A bucket of leagues inside a sport, forming the top tier of the league directory.

fixtureCount.description: All fixtures in the category’s leagues on the UTC day, regardless of state.

leagueCount.description: Number of the category’s leagues that have one or more fixtures that day.

Coverage.description: The scope of the API in figures: how many entities carry a DataSportsAPI id, what each sport’s league directory holds and how far back its headline competitions go.

updatedAt.description: Time these figures were computed (ISO 8601). The totals are refreshed every hour, the per-sport directories once a day.

sports.description: Number of sports served — the same list as GET /v2/sports.

totals.description: Counts of the entities that have a DataSportsAPI id, each of which can be fetched by that id. The numbers only rise: an id, once issued, is never changed or withdrawn.

history.description: How deep the headline competitions of all sports go, taken together.

bySport.description: One entry per sport whose directory has been read, in the order of /v2/sports. Shortly after this endpoint is redeployed a sport can be absent until its directory has been read once.

CoverageTotals.description: Counts of the entities that have a DataSportsAPI id, each of which can be fetched by that id. The numbers only rise: an id, once issued, is never changed or withdrawn.

leagues.description: Competitions and leagues that have a DataSportsAPI id.

seasons.description: League seasons that have a DataSportsAPI id.

teams.description: Teams that have a DataSportsAPI id: clubs and national sides, plus the individual competitors of one-on-one sports such as tennis, MMA, darts and snooker.

players.description: Players that have a DataSportsAPI id.

fixtures.description: Fixtures (matches), played and upcoming, that have a DataSportsAPI id.

venues.description: Venues that have a DataSportsAPI id.

managers.description: Managers and head coaches that have a DataSportsAPI id.

referees.description: Referees that have a DataSportsAPI id.

CoverageHistory.description: A summary of how deep the headline competitions of all sports go.

leagues.description: Number of headline competitions (the `headline` lists of every sport) whose firstSeason is known.

medianYears.description: Median number of years between those competitions’ first season and the current year; null when no first season is known.

oldestSeason.description: Earliest firstSeason among those competitions; null when none is known.

SportCoverage.description: One sport’s league directory in numbers, and how far back its headline competitions go.

sport.description: Slug of the sport, as listed by /v2/sports.

kind.description: The endpoint family that serves this sport’s data.

categories.description: Number of categories (countries, regions, tours or games) the sport’s league directory holds (GET /v2/categories?sport=).

leagues.description: Number of leagues across all those categories (GET /v2/leagues?category=); motorsport and cycling count series instead (GET /v2/series?category=).

historyFrom.description: Earliest firstSeason found in `headline`; null if unknown.

headline.description: Up to ten headline competitions for the sport: the popular international competitions in its directory or, failing those, the first leagues of the directory, in that order.

CoverageLeague.description: One headline competition of a sport, with the depth of its season list.

id.description: League id issued by DataSportsAPI (for motorsport and cycling, a series id).

name.description: Name of the league, competition or series.

seasons.description: How many seasons its season list holds (GET /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons; motorsport and cycling use /v2/series/{id}/seasons).

firstSeason.description: Start year of the oldest season in that list; null when no season label can be parsed. Older seasons carry less detail: results and tables usually reach further back than lineups and statistics.

PlayerActions.description: A player’s on-ball actions in one match, each placed on the pitch — the same actions our data source’s player rating is built from (football, covered leagues). When the source has none (the player did not play, the match has not started, or it is another sport) the response is 200 with empty lists.

passes.description: Passes and crosses in our data source’s order (no timestamps are provided).

defensive.description: Defensive actions: tackles, interceptions, ball recoveries, clearances and blocks.

ballCarries.description: Ball carries, i.e. runs made in possession.

PlayerAction.description: Describes one thing a player did on the ball in a match.

start.description: Player’s location when the action began.

end.description: End point: where the ball travelled to (passes, crosses, clearances) or where it was carried (ball carries). Null for other action types and when our data source has none.

successful.description: Whether the action succeeded — a completed pass or cross, a take-on or tackle won. Our data source marks successes only, so anything else reads false (we checked this against accuratePass / wonContest / wonTackle in the lineups). Ball carries have no outcome and get null.

keyPass.description: `true` for a pass or cross that set up a shot. Null for other action types.

longBall.description: `true` when our data source counts it as a long ball (passes and crosses); these flags can add up to more than totalLongBalls in the lineups. Null for other action types.

ActionPoint.description: Pitch coordinates marking where an action began or finished.

x.description: Position along the pitch, 0–100, oriented in the player’s attacking direction (0 at the player’s own goal line, 100 at the goal they are attacking). Both sides use this frame, the same as the match heatmap. Unit: percent.

y.description: Widthwise position on the pitch, 0–100, using the heatmap’s frame. Unit: percent.

RaceLap.description: Lap data for one competitor on one lap of a race session.

lap.description: Number of the lap; 0 represents the starting grid.

position.description: Position when the lap ended (on lap 0, the grid slot); null on the lap where the competitor retired.

pitStop.description: `true` if the competitor pitted at the end of this lap (the new tyres appear from the next lap).

retired.description: `true` if the competitor retired during this lap, making it their final one (`position` is null).

RaceCompetitorLaps.description: A competitor’s race broken down lap by lap, showing position, tyre and pit stops for each lap.

competitor.description: Driver for this record — a TeamRef of kind individual, resolvable via /v2/teams/{id}.

team.description: Constructor the driver races for.

laps.description: Starts with lap 0 (the grid), followed by each lap completed in sequence; for a competitor who retired, the list ends at that lap.

PlayerStatRanking.description: A player’s league-season rank for a single statistic.

statistic.description: Statistic being ranked, named as in /v2/players/{id}/statistics (goals, assists, rating, expectedGoals, …).

value.description: Player’s value for this statistic across the league season.

rank.description: The player’s rank for this statistic among all league players (1 = top). Equal values share the same rank, as in standard competition ranking.

tiedCount.description: How many players hold that rank, including them (1 means no tie).

playerCount.description: Size of the ranked field for this statistic in the league season.

GoalDistribution.description: The timing of a team’s goals scored and conceded across a league season (football).

scored.description: Goals the team scored in those matches.

conceded.description: Goals the team conceded in those matches.

bands.description: Six bands of 15 minutes each, in chronological order.

GoalDistributionBand.description: Goal counts for a single 15-minute slice of the match.

fromMinute.description: Minute at which the band starts (1, 16, 31, …). Unit: minutes.

toMinute.description: Minute at which the band ends (15, 30, … 90). Stoppage time is counted in the band it is added to. Unit: minutes.

scored.description: Goals scored by the team in this band.

conceded.description: Goals conceded by the team in this band.

TennisYearStatistics.description: Figures for a tennis player covering one calendar year and one surface.

surface.description: Court surface the figures relate to.

firstServePointsWon.description: Service points won after landing the first serve.

secondServes.description: Service points that needed a second serve.

secondServesIn.description: Count of second serves that went in (= secondServes − doubleFaults).

secondServePointsWon.description: Service points won when playing on a second serve.

breakPointsConverted.description: Break points they converted while returning serve.

breakPointChances.description: Break-point chances they created while returning serve.

breakPointsFaced.description: Break points they had to defend while serving.

breakPointsLost.description: Of the break points against them, how many the opponent won.

LeagueChampion.description: The champion of a single league season.

seasonId.description: Id of the season in question, matching a Season from /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons.

year.description: Year in which the season finished (2026 for 25/26).

team.description: Team that took the title.

Odds.description: Betting prices for a fixture from a single bookmaker, supplied via our data source; the prices carry no bookmaker identity. Pre-match and in-play, opening and current, plus settlement flags once the match is over. Available since 2026-11-04. Live updates arrive on the `odds:{fixtureId}` WebSocket channel (on Business and Enterprise). These are third-party prices shown for information only — they are neither advice nor an offer to bet.

updatedAt.description: Our last fetch or receipt of these prices (no timestamp comes from our data source itself); null when no prices exist.

markets.description: All markets the bookmaker offers on the fixture, in the bookmaker’s order. Empty when there are none — typically a minor league, a match far in the future, or a finished match whose odds have been removed.

OddsMarket.description: A market the bookmaker offers for a fixture.

key.description: Identifier of the market that stays stable within its fixture. It is built from `kind`, followed by `:period` unless the market covers the whole match, `:line` if there is a line, and `:live` for in-play markets ("result", "result:half1", "totalGoals:2.5", "asianHandicap:-1.25", "winner:live"). For `other` markets the label is added ("other:corners-1x2"), and further markets sharing a key get `#2`, `#3`. The `:live` suffix exists because, once play starts, the bookmaker shows the in-play market alongside the closed pre-match one. When a line moves it gets a new key and the old key disappears. Use this key to merge WebSocket `odds` frames.

name.description: Market name as the bookmaker labels it ("Full time", "Match goals", "Asian handicap").

period.description: Portion of the match the market is settled on: "match" when it covers the whole match in the market’s own sense (see `kind`); otherwise a unit with a number — half1, half2, quarter1…4, period1…3 (ice hockey), set1…, inning1…, map1…, game1…, round1…. Whatever the sport’s division, a half always means half of the match (in basketball, half1 = quarters 1–2). null if our data source’s period label is not recognised (check `name`).

line.description: Line value: the over / under threshold for a total, or the home side’s handicap for a handicap market. Null for markets without a line.

live.description: `true` for in-play prices — once the match has started and the bookmaker is trading it live.

suspended.description: `true` while a goal, red card, VAR check or similar has paused the market; the prices shown cannot be bet on at that moment.

choices.description: Selections in the bookmaker’s order: home ahead of away, with draw / "no goal" between them.

settledBy.description: Who set the `winning` flags of its choices: `source` (the bookmaker’s own flags) or `computed` (settled on our side from the final result, since the bookmaker never sends flags for it — football Asian handicaps on half lines, judged on the regular-time score, and total cards when every card of the match was a yellow one shown to a player on the pitch and the incidents agree with the statistics). Null while nobody has settled it. Since 2026-11-12.

OddsChoice.description: A single selection within a betting market, together with its price.

name.description: Label the bookmaker uses for the selection, as passed on by our data source ("1", "X", "Over", "(-0.5) Galatasaray", a team name).

fractional.description: Current price in fractional form ("19/20" means 19 profit for every 20 staked). null while the bookmaker displays no price.

decimal.description: Decimal form of the current price (= 1 + fractional, which is the total paid back per unit staked), rounded to two decimal places. Null exactly when `fractional` is null.

openingFractional.description: Opening price of the market, in fractional form.

openingDecimal.description: Opening price of the market, in decimal form.

change.description: Direction of the price’s most recent movement.

winning.description: Once settled, `true` if this selection won. Null before settlement, and on markets that nobody settles (see the market’s `settledBy`).

FeaturedOdds.description: The headline market for a fixture in a daily odds list — the three-way result in sports that allow draws, otherwise the winner market.

fixtureId.description: The fixture’s id; GET /v2/fixtures/{id} returns the match and GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/odds returns all of its markets.

market.description: A market the bookmaker offers for a fixture.

WinningOdds.description: Winning-odds figures for a fixture. It takes each side’s win price (from one bookmaker, via our data source) and gives the probability that price implies plus how often sides at that price have won in the past — both figures come from the data source. It is two-way only, so there is no draw entry. Available since 2026-11-06. The prices and statistics come from a third party and are for information only; they are not advice or an offer to bet.

updatedAt.description: Time we last fetched the figures (our data source supplies no timestamp of its own); null if there are no figures.

home.description: Figures for the home side; null if our data source has none for it (it may cover only one side).

away.description: Figures for the away side; null if our data source has none for it.

WinningOddsSide.description: A side’s win price alongside the historical success rate of that price.

fractional.description: The side’s win price that the figures are based on, fractional ("33/20"). Our data source chooses this pre-match price itself, so it may not match any current or opening price from GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/odds.

decimal.description: Decimal equivalent of that price (= 1 + fractional), rounded to two decimal places.

expectedWinPercentage.description: Implied probability of winning at this price, 0–100 (≈ 100 / decimal, rounded by our data source, with the bookmaker’s margin left in). Unit: percent.

actualWinPercentage.description: Historical win rate for sides at this price, 0–100, from the data source’s own records (it discloses neither the sample size nor the time span). Unit: percent.

LiveWireEvent.description: What the `livescores` channel published, one change at a time, stored for 7 days: goals and other score changes, red cards, kick-offs, period starts, breaks and final whistles. Each comes with the score and status that followed it and both sides’ names, so a ticker has something to show before its socket delivers a frame.

fixtureId.description: The fixture’s id in our system (/v2/fixtures/{id}).

sport.description: The sport slug, as listed by /v2/sports.

leagueId.description: The id we give the fixture’s league; null if it has none.

kind.description: What happened. A moment has exactly one kind: the first that fits, in the order score, redCard, finished, break, kickoff, period.

at.description: The time we published this change on the `livescores` channel.

side.description: For score and redCard, the side whose count changed (null if both changed); null for every other kind.

homeScore.description: The home side’s `current` score just after the change; null if the fixture had no score.

awayScore.description: The away side’s `current` score just after the change.

status.description: The fixture’s status just after the change (`type`, `phase` and `period`, as on Fixture).

home.description: The home side; null until it is known.

away.description: The away side; null until it is known.

LiveWireTeam.description: One side of a live-wire moment, named as the fixture named it at that time.

id.description: The team’s id in our system.

name.description: The team’s name (in individual sports the player, or both players of a doubles pair).

TrackingSummary.description: Which tracking data a fixture holds. In football: a ball track and events recorded live (goals, shots, cards, set pieces, the flow of play), completed after the final whistle by the full event list including passes and positions. In tennis: every serve and every point and the positions of ball and players, all live. In basketball: a live timeline with shot spots, and events read after the match. In ice hockey: a live timeline showing where the shots came from. In darts (since 2026-11-13): a live timeline of every dart and every visit. History starts on 2026-11-07 for every sport.

sport.description: One of the five sports with tracking data, as a slug (football, tennis, basketball, ice-hockey, darts); darts since 2026-11-13.

coordinates.description: The coordinate frame for this fixture, which depends on the sport; every x / y / z the tracking endpoints return is expressed in it.

final.description: True once the match is over — finished, or ended another way (canceled, postponed, interrupted, abandoned); no further ball frames will be added.

complete.description: True once the post-match data has been read, from a few minutes to an hour after the end; from then on the tracked events, the timeline and the player names are final. Until then football has only its live events — goals, shots, cards, substitutions, set pieces and the flow of play, with passes and most of the detail arriving in the post-match read — while basketball, ice hockey and darts have their live timeline (since 2026-11-13).

startedAt.description: Start of recording, close to kick-off.

ballFrames.description: Count of ball frames recorded so far (see GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/tracking/ball): about 14 per minute of football play, about one per tennis shot. They are captured live only, so a frame missed during play never turns up later.

events.description: Count of events served by GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/tracking/events so far.

timelineEvents.description: How many timeline events exist (basketball, ice hockey and darts; GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/tracking/timeline).

players.description: True if the match has player tracking (since 2026-11-13): the ball and every player on the court, five times per second (GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/tracking/players and the playerFrame frame). Only NBA games have it; it is false everywhere else.

TrackingSpot.description: A spot expressed in the coordinate frame of the fixture (see TrackingSummary.coordinates).

x.description: Position along the pitch, court or rink, in the fixture’s frame (TrackingCoordinates).

y.description: Position across the pitch, court or rink, in that same frame.

z.description: Height of the tennis ball above the court in millimetres (tennis ball positions only); null elsewhere.

BallFrame.description: One position from the live ball track (tennis and football).

at.description: Moment the ball was recorded at this spot, to the millisecond.
