x.description: Position along the pitch or court in the fixture’s frame (0–100 in football, millimetres in tennis); null when no position came from the source.

y.description: Position across it, in the same frame. In football it runs the same way as the tracked events’ position.y (since 2026-11-13).

TrackedEvent.description: One entry of the tracked play-by-play, with where it happened (football, tennis, basketball). Tennis and football are delivered live — football roughly 9 seconds after the moment (about 15 at most) for goals, shots, cards, substitutions, set pieces and the flow of play, while passes and most of the detail follow in the post-match read. Basketball events mostly come later, with the post-match read of the data.

key.description: Key that identifies the event within the fixture and never changes; REST and WebSocket use the same key.

type.description: What happened, in camelCase. Football: goal, attemptAtGoal, pass, cross, dribble, corner, freeKick, throwIn, goalKick, penalty, foul, offside, duel, tackle, interception, clearance, block, save, yellowCard, secondYellowCard, redCard, substitution; flowAttack / flowDangerousAttack / flowBallSafe describe the flow of play (side is the team in possession, position is where the ball is — together, the live state of the match); possibleCorner / possibleGoal / possiblePenalty (and the matching …Cancelled types) mark a decision still pending; possessionChange has no side; also kickOff, periodStatus, injuryTime, injury, backFromInjury, interruptionStart / interruptionOver, videoReview and more. Tennis: serve, fault, let, point, challenge, ballSituation (where the ball is), playerSituation (where a player is) and more. Basketball: freeThrow, twoPointer, threePointer, rebound, steal, block, turnover, foul, possessionChange, substitutionIn / substitutionOut, timeoutStart, periodStatus and more. Further types may appear; ignore any you do not recognise, or show it as information only.

side.description: Side credited with the event; null for neutral ones such as a period change or a loose ball.

minute.description: Football: match minute. Null for other sports. Unit: minutes.

second.description: Football: match clock in seconds. Null for other sports. Unit: seconds.

period.description: Basketball: period in which it happened (period1…period4, overtime). Null for other sports.

game.description: Tennis: game number in the set.

position.description: Location of the event: for football (pass origin, shot, foul, …) and basketball (shot, foul, rebound, …) on the 0–100 frame; for tennis ballSituation / playerSituation in millimetres, with z as the ball’s height. Null when the source gives no spot.

endPosition.description: Football passes: the spot the ball was played to.

player.description: Who performed it, if the source names someone the squad list contains.

assist.description: Football goals: who provided the assist.

outcome.description: Result, in camelCase: complete / incomplete for passes; onTarget, offTarget, blocked, woodwork, deflectedOffTarget and more for shots; made / missed in basketball.

goalType.description: Football goals: how it was scored, in camelCase (shot, header, ownGoal, penalty, …).

gameScore.description: Tennis points: the score in the game once the point was played.

pointOutcome.description: Tennis points: how the point was won, in camelCase (standard, ace, doubleFault, …).

shots.description: Tennis points: number of shots in the rally, when provided.

TrackedPlayer.description: A player that a tracked event names, taken from the match squad. There is no id: tracked players are not linked to DataSportsAPI player ids.

name.description: Name as displayed, given name first.

shirtNumber.description: Number on their shirt in this match.

side.description: Which side the player is on.

TennisGameScore.description: The score within a tennis game after a point.

home.description: Home side’s points in the current game — 0, 15, 30, 40 or A (advantage) — or the tie-break count.

away.description: Points of the away side in the game.

TimelineEvent.description: One entry of a match timeline in basketball, ice hockey or darts: shots with where they were taken, saves, penalties, goals and periods, and in darts each dart and each visit. Live since 2026-11-13, roughly 5 seconds after the moment (also pushed as timelineEvent frames on tracking:{id}); the source can still revise or withdraw an event afterwards. Events the source withdrew are not included.

key.description: Key that identifies the event within the fixture and never changes.

type.description: Event type as the source names it, in camelCase. Basketball: goal (a made basket; points gives its value), attemptMissed, freeThrowsAwarded, rebound, block, stealBasket, turnoverBasket, foul, wonJumpBall, timeout, tvTimeoutStart / tvTimeoutStop, videoReview, periodStart, periodScore, matchStarted, matchEnded and more. Ice hockey: goal, canceledEvent (a goal that was taken back), shotOnTarget, goalkeeperSaved, shotOffTarget, shotBlocked, faceoff, giveaway, takeaway, hit, suspension (a penalty; penaltyMinutes gives its length), suspensionOver, delayedPenalty, emptyNet, emptyNetOver, playResumesAfterGoal, timeout, periodStart, periodBreak (an intermission, or the wait before overtime; period is null), periodScore, penalty (a shoot-out attempt, with homeScore / awayScore giving the shoot-out score once it is taken), penaltyRewarded / penaltyMissed (penalty shots) and more. Darts (since 2026-11-13; the detail is in darts): dartThrow (a single dart), visit (a turn at the board, at most three darts), checkout (the visit that closed out the leg), legWon (homeScore / awayScore count legs), setWon, matchWon, throwsFirst, periodStart, matchStarted, matchEnded. Other types may be added.

name.description: The source’s English label for the event (“Goalie save”, “1st period”, “2 pt scored”).

side.description: Side credited with the event; null when neutral.

second.description: Game clock, in seconds from the start. Unit: seconds.

period.description: For periodStart / periodScore: the number of the period.

position.description: Where the shot or event happened, 0–100, in a frame where home plays towards x = 100 and away towards x = 0 for the whole match (TrackingCoordinates court or rink). The source does not report attack direction, so for each side and period, when that side’s shots sit in the wrong half (x < 50 for home, x > 50 for away), all its positions in that period are mirrored (x → 100 − x, y → 100 − y); when a side has no shots in a period, it borrows the direction from the other side and from the adjacent periods. Null when the source gives no spot.

player.description: Name of the player involved (the scorer of a goal), with the first name first, if the source gives a name.

assists.description: Names of the players credited with assists on a goal, in order.

points.description: Basketball: what the shot was worth (1, 2 or 3).

penaltyMinutes.description: Ice hockey suspensions: length of the penalty. Unit: minutes.

homeScore.description: Home side’s score once the event is applied (goals, period scores, end of match). On a shoot-out attempt in ice hockey (type penalty) it is the shoot-out tally after that attempt (since 2026-11-13).

awayScore.description: Away side’s score once the event is applied.

darts.description: Darts (since 2026-11-13): the dart or the visit. Null for other sports, and for darts events that are not a dart or a visit.

TimelineDarts.description: Darts detail on a timeline entry (since 2026-11-13): either one dart (dartThrow) or one visit together with what it settled (visit, checkout, setWon, matchWon); any field that does not apply is null. Some competitions only report visits, without the individual darts.

score.description: dartThrow: points the dart scored (0 – 60). visit / checkout: total of the visit (0 – 180).

number.description: dartThrow: the segment number hit (1 – 20, or 25 for the bull); null when the dart missed.

multiplier.description: dartThrow: 1 for a single, 2 for a double or the bullseye, 3 for a treble, 0 for a miss.

ring.description: dartThrow: the part of the board it landed in.

bed.description: dartThrow in a single (since 2026-11-13): which single bed it hit, inner (from the outer bull to the treble) or outer (from the treble to the double), as reported by the source. Null for any other ring, any other event type, and a single the source does not locate.

doubleAttempt.description: dartThrow: true when the dart was aimed at a finishing double.

dartsThrown.description: visit / checkout: how many darts the visit used (1 – 3).

checkoutDouble.description: checkout: the double that won the leg (16 means double 16, 25 the bullseye).

remaining.description: visit: points each side still needs in this leg once the visit is counted.

legs.description: visit / checkout / setWon / matchWon: legs won so far, counted within the current set if the match uses sets.

sets.description: visit / checkout / setWon / matchWon: number of sets won; a legs-only match counts as one single set.

DartsScore.description: A darts figure for each side: points left, legs or sets.

TrackingSnapshot.description: Snapshot of a tracking:{id} channel: the summary, the most recent ball frames, tracked events and timeline entries, together with the latest player frame; anything older is available over REST.

tracking.description: What has been recorded for the fixture so far; null while nothing is recorded yet (an untracked match, or one that has not started).

ball.description: The latest ball frames, at most 100, oldest first.

events.description: The latest tracked events, at most 100, oldest first.

timeline.description: Since 2026-11-13: the latest timeline events, at most 100, oldest first, in basketball, ice hockey and darts; an empty list in other sports.

playerFrame.description: The most recent player frame, for NBA games (since 2026-11-13); null when the match has no player tracking. Every playerFrame frame replaces it.

PlayerFrame.description: A single player-tracking frame, for basketball and only in NBA games (since 2026-11-13): the ball and all players on the court, five frames per second. Positions use the court frame with home attacking the x = 100 basket throughout; the teams change ends at half-time, the frame does not. Which way each team plays is worked out per period from where its shots go, so a live frame from the opening seconds of a match, before anyone has shot, may come mirrored; frames read again over REST are corrected. Half-time has no frames (warm-ups are dropped). Recorded live only: a game that was not captured live has no frames.

frame.description: Rising frame counter for the match (gaps are expected). It gives the order and is the paging cursor (after) of GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/tracking/players.

at.description: Time we received the frame, roughly 1–2 s later than the moment it depicts. Frames come in batches of five per second that share this time: show them in `frame` order with 0.2 s between them.

period.description: Period number: 1–4 are the quarters, 5 is the first overtime, 6 the second, and so on.

clock.description: Game clock: seconds remaining in the period. Unit: seconds.

shotClock.description: Shot clock in seconds; null while it is switched off. Unit: seconds.

running.description: True while the game clock is ticking.

possession.description: The side and player in possession; null when neither side has the ball.

ball.description: Ball position; null when the tracker cannot see it.

players.description: Everyone on the court (ten during play).

PlayerFramePossession.description: Ball possession within a player frame.

player.description: Player holding the ball; null when nobody holds it (a shot in flight, a loose ball) or when the squad has no entry for them.

PlayerFrameBall.description: Ball position within a player frame.

x.description: Along the court, 0–100 (TrackingCoordinates court, home shooting at x = 100).

height.description: Metres above the floor (the rim sits at 3.05).

PlayerFramePlayer.description: One player on the floor, as seen in a player frame. There is no id, because tracked players are not linked to DataSportsAPI player ids; within one match, name, shirt number and side tell them apart.

side.description: Which side the player is on; null if the match squad does not include them.

name.description: Name as displayed, given name first; null if the match squad does not include them.

shirtNumber.description: Number on their shirt in this match.

x.description: Position along the court on the 0–100 court frame; slightly beyond that range while the player has stepped off the floor (out of bounds, by the bench).

y.description: Across the court, 0–100, in the same way.

WsWelcome.description: The server sends this frame first, as soon as the connection opens.

protocol.description: Version of the protocol in use. It has been 4 since the evening of 2026-10-23 (from then on, a fixture joining a list channel is delivered as a `fixture` frame); it was 3 from 2026-10-23 and 2 from 2026-10-19. Channels and frame types are added without changing this number (odds:{id} on 2026-11-04, tracking:{id} on 2026-11-12, the timelineEvent and playerFrame frames on tracking:{id} on 2026-11-13), so skip any frame type you do not recognise.

heartbeatMs.description: Interval between server pings. Reply to them (browsers do this automatically) or the connection is closed.

maxChannels.description: Maximum number of channels this connection may subscribe to.

replay.description: True when your plan includes `lastSeq` replay.

WsSnapshot.description: The complete current state of a channel, delivered when you subscribe and again whenever you resync.

seq.description: Current sequence number of the channel. Treat it as an opaque, increasing counter that does not start at 0; the following delta carries seq + 1.

data.description: Depends on the channel. livescores / sport:{slug} / league:{id} / team:{id} carry a Fixture[]: for league:{id}, that league’s in-progress fixtures; for team:{id} (since 2026-11-04), that team’s in-progress fixtures, home and away. fixture:{id} carries a Fixture and race:{id} a RaceSnapshot; odds:{id} (since 2026-11-04) carries an Odds matching GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/odds, and tracking:{id} (since 2026-11-12) a TrackingSnapshot. Each of these four is null when there is no data.

WsDelta.description: Sent when a single fixture changes. On the four list channels (livescores, sport:{slug}, league:{id}, team:{id}), every delta concerns a fixture the channel already sent you, either in its snapshot or as a `fixture` frame, and a fixture that drops out of the channel (finished, canceled) receives one final delta reporting that. Deltas cover both live-feed updates and the corrections a board refresh produces. A score that goes DOWN (a goal disallowed, a basket corrected) arrives within 1.5 s of the source sending it; the delay lets us drop the brief flaps when the source re-sends an older score. A REST refetch of /fixtures/{id} may still be a few seconds ahead, so resync from time to time if you need exact values.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel. A gap means you lost a delta — send resync.

changes.description: A partial Fixture that uses the same field names and nesting as the full object. Deep-merge it into the Fixture you store: objects are merged key by key, while every other value (null included) overwrites what you have. No fields beyond those listed for FixturePatch are ever sent.

WsFixture.description: On the four list channels (livescores, sport:{slug}, league:{id}, team:{id}): the channel’s set gained a fixture — after kick-off, or when the server first sees it. The frame carries the complete Fixture, exactly as a snapshot would contain it. Append it to your list and apply subsequent deltas to it. fixture:{id} channels never receive this frame.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel; the counter is shared with deltas.

data.description: A match, in the same shape used by every endpoint and by WebSocket snapshots.

WsSubscribed.description: Acknowledges a subscribe that produced no snapshot: either a `lastSeq` replay (sent once the replayed frames have gone out) or a repeat subscribe to a channel you already hold.

seq.description: Current seq of the channel once the replay is done; the following delta carries seq + 1.

replayed.description: Number of frames the replay delivered. 0 means you missed nothing, or that you were already subscribed to the channel.

WsWinProbability.description: On fixture:{id} channels for football fixtures in play: the win-probability estimate shifted by one percentage point or more (evaluated whenever the fixture changes and once per minute). `point` matches the endpoint’s `current`, including why it moved, and `point.at` is the moment it was calculated. It is NOT a point on the stored curve, whose per-minute points fall at the end of each minute; for a chart, fetch GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/win-probability once and then refresh it with `?since=`.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel; the channel’s deltas use the same counter.

sport.description: Slug of the fixture’s sport; win probability exists only for football.

model.description: Version of the model that produced the estimate. Each version is described in the docs, and new ones are announced in the changelog.

point.description: One point on the win-probability curve: the estimate together with the reason it was produced.

WsCommentary.description: On fixture:{id} channels for football fixtures: a fresh AI commentary entry has been produced. Keep the two counters apart: the frame’s `seq` belongs to the channel (and is shared with deltas), whereas `entry.seq` numbers the entry within GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/commentary.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel; the channel’s deltas use the same counter.

sport.description: Slug of the fixture’s sport; commentary exists only for football.

WsEvents.description: On fixture:{id} channels for fixtures in play: the list of match events (goals, cards, substitutions, VAR decisions, periods, …) has changed. Because the live feed contains no events, the server pulls them from REST: roughly 20 s and 45 s after every change of score, red cards or status (goals reach the source’s event list 18–33 s after the score changes), and every 30 s during play, since cards and substitutions trigger no signal. A frame goes out only when the list differs. A disallowed goal shows up in `changes.removed`, and only after REST has confirmed it. Each frame holds the complete list, so missing one does no harm; fetch GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/events for the state before the first frame arrives.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel; the channel’s deltas use the same counter.

events.description: The FULL events list as it stands, in chronological order — the incidents GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/events returns, keys included. Replace your copy with it.

changes.description: The difference between this events frame and the one before it.

WsStatistics.description: On fixture:{id} channels for fixtures in play: the match statistics have changed, and the frame carries the complete object as returned by GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/statistics. The server reads REST every 30 s while at least one client is subscribed, plus a final read after full time, and emits a frame only when the content differs. Figures typically trail the action by ~30–60 s.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel; the channel’s deltas use the same counter.

statistics.description: The match statistics, broken down by period.

WsLineups.description: On fixture:{id} channels for fixtures in play: the lineups have changed. The frame carries the whole object that GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups returns, including each player’s statistics. While someone is subscribed the server checks every 30 s, stopping once the lineups are confirmed and have stayed the same for 10 minutes. Substitutions are delivered as events instead.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel; the channel’s deltas use the same counter.

WsPlayByPlay.description: On fixture:{id} channels, for football and basketball matches in play: the source’s play-by-play commentary has new or changed text. While at least one client is subscribed the server re-reads REST every 20 s (the source’s own page updates every 15–20 s), and once more after full time. A frame is sent only when the list differs, and it starts at the first entry that changed. For the state before the first frame, call GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/play-by-play.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel; the channel’s deltas use the same counter.

start.description: 0-based position, in the full list, of the first item in `entries`. Retain your first `start` entries, discard everything after them and append `entries`. Normally equal to the length of your list (new lines added at the end); lower when the source edited or deleted a line.

total.description: Current length of the full list (start + entries.length). If `start` is beyond the end of your list, you are out of sync — reload GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/play-by-play.

entries.description: Entries from position `start` onwards, oldest first, in the form GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/play-by-play returns them.

WsMomentum.description: On fixture:{id} channels for football fixtures in play: the momentum graph has changed. The frame holds the complete object as returned by GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/momentum; with one point per minute, expect roughly one frame a minute. While anyone is subscribed the server checks every 30 s (and once more after full time) and only sends a frame if something changed.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel; the channel’s deltas use the same counter.

momentum.description: The momentum graph: a value per game in tennis, or per minute in football, basketball, handball, ice hockey and the like.

WsShotmap.description: On fixture:{id} channels for football fixtures in play: the shot map has changed, through either a new shot or a correction by the source. While anyone is subscribed the server checks every 30 s (and once more after full time) and only sends a frame if something changed. Shots typically appear ~30–60 s after they happen.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel; the channel’s deltas use the same counter.

shots.description: The current shot map in FULL, oldest first, as returned by GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/shotmap. Overwrite your copy with it.

WsRace.description: On race:{id}: something about the race changed, such as a session starting or finishing, or a status or schedule update. The frame carries the complete Race as returned by GET /v2/races/{id}. Since the live feed has no data for race sports, the server reads REST every 60 s while a session is running or due to begin within 15 minutes.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel.

sport.description: Slug of the race’s sport (motorsport, cycling).

data.description: A race: a motorsport weekend with practice, qualifying, sprint and race, or a cycling event — one-day or stage race.

WsRaceResults.description: On race:{id}: the classification of a session has changed. The server checks every 30 s while the session is running and one last time when it finishes, and sends a frame only when something differs.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel.

session.description: The session this classification belongs to.

results.description: The full classification of the session, as returned by /v2/races/{id}/results?session=.

WsOdds.description: On odds:{fixtureId}: prices have moved (available since 2026-11-04). Price changes, both in-play and pre-match, come from the source’s live odds feed and reach you within roughly a second. Suspensions, newly added markets and settlement flags rely on a REST re-read, every 30 s during the match and every 2 minutes beforehand. Hold on to the snapshot (an Odds, as returned by GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/odds) and merge every frame into it by market `key`. Odds travel exclusively on `odds:{id}`; no other channel includes them.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel.

updatedAt.description: Time at which these prices came in.

markets.description: Markets that changed, each sent in FULL with all its choices. Swap out your market with the matching `key`, or add it if you do not have one yet.

removed.description: Keys of markets the bookmaker has withdrawn (for example a handicap line that moved, or a closed market). Remove them from your copy.

WsBall.description: On tracking:{fixtureId} (since 2026-11-12): one new position of the live ball track — about 14 a minute of football play, about one per tennis shot — sent within roughly a second after the source records it. Add it to the end of the ball list you got with the snapshot.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel.

frame.description: The new position of the ball (football, tennis).

WsTrackedEvent.description: On tracking:{fixtureId} (since 2026-11-12): one more tracked event. Tennis sends each serve, point, ball position and player position live. Football sends, live and about 18 a minute, its goals, shots, cards, substitutions, set pieces and the flow-of-play types (possessionChange, flowAttack, flowDangerousAttack, flowBallSafe), then the passes in one burst with the post-match read. Basketball events come mostly in that burst. Keep events keyed by key; receiving a key you already have means the same event again.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel.

event.description: A tracked play-by-play event and where on the pitch or court it happened (football, tennis, basketball). Tennis events are sent live; football ones too, usually some 9 seconds behind play and rarely past 15 (flow of play, set pieces, shots, goals, cards, substitutions, while passes and finer detail follow with the post-match read). Basketball events mostly come with the post-match read.

WsTimelineEvent.description: On tracking:{fixtureId} (since 2026-11-13): one basketball, ice hockey or darts timeline event, roughly 5 seconds after the moment (about 4 – 8 a minute in basketball, about 25 – 30 in darts). With upsert, add it or overwrite the one under the same key (a revision; earlier positions in a period can shift once its shots show which way the side attacks); with remove, the source has withdrawn it. Start from the snapshot’s timeline and apply every frame by key.

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel.

op.description: How this frame changes the timeline you keep.

key.description: Key of the event (TimelineEvent.key) to add, overwrite or delete.

event.description: For upsert, the event; null for remove.

WsPlayerFrame.description: On tracking:{fixtureId}, NBA games only (since 2026-11-13): one player frame with the ball and every player, five per second, about 1–2 seconds behind play and delivered in batches of five each second. Unlike every other frame it has NO seq and is never replayed: it samples the current state and the newest frame wins. Replace the snapshot’s playerFrame with it, and show the frames of one batch in `frame` order, spacing them 0.2 s. A connection that lags behind receives the newer frames and misses the older ones.

frame.description: One player-tracking frame (basketball, NBA games only; since 2026-11-13): the ball and every player on the court, five frames a second, in a court frame where the home side attacks x = 100 in every period, although the teams swap baskets at half-time. Each team’s direction is read per period from where its shots go up, so a live frame from the first seconds, before any shot, can arrive mirrored (a later REST read is corrected). No frames during half-time, and none for a game that was not recorded live.

WsTrackingStatus.description: On tracking:{fixtureId} (since 2026-11-12): sent when the match ends (final) and again when its post-match data has been read (complete).

seq.description: One more than the previous seq on this channel.

final.description: The match has ended; the ball track is closed.

complete.description: The post-match data has been read: call the REST tracking endpoints again to get the settled events, timeline and player names.

WsUnsubscribed.description: Acknowledges that you have left a channel.

WsPing.description: Heartbeat at the application level, emitted every heartbeatMs alongside the protocol-level ping. You do not need to answer it.

WsPong.description: The server’s answer to a { "type": "ping" } you sent.

WsError.description: The server rejected a frame you sent. Your connection remains open.

code.description: Machine-readable code of the WebSocket error.

Side.description: One of the two sides in a fixture.

x-enumDescriptions.home: The side listed as home in the fixture.
x-enumDescriptions.away: The side listed as away in the fixture.

Winner.description: Outcome of a fixture that has finished.

x-enumDescriptions.draw: Neither side won; the fixture was drawn.

StatusType.description: High-level state of a match, meant for filtering.

x-enumDescriptions.notstarted: Has not begun yet: still scheduled, or its start has been delayed.
x-enumDescriptions.inprogress: Under way, breaks included (for example half-time, or a fight waiting for its decision).
x-enumDescriptions.interrupted: Halted partway through (weather, crowd, …); play is expected to restart.
x-enumDescriptions.willcontinue: A match spread over several days, currently between days (for cricket Tests, the end of day N).
x-enumDescriptions.postponed: Rescheduled for a later date; the fixture id stays the same.
x-enumDescriptions.canceled: The match is not going to be played (canceled, abandoned or removed).

StatusPhase.description: Detailed match state, as a scoreboard would display it.

x-enumDescriptions.notstarted: Scheduled and not yet under way.
x-enumDescriptions.delayed: The start time has passed but play has been delayed.
x-enumDescriptions.inprogress: A period is in play; status.period identifies which one.
x-enumDescriptions.break: A planned stoppage within the match, such as half-time, the gap between sets, waiting for extra time or penalties, or a cricket lunch / tea / drinks interval.

WinProbabilityModel.description: Versions of the win-probability model. Each version is explained below, and any new one is announced in the changelog.

x-enumDescriptions.v1: The original model (2026-10-22). Its pre-match estimate relies solely on the current competition’s table and form. Fixtures whose pre-match estimate was locked in before v2 still use it, since the estimate is kept once a match starts.
x-enumDescriptions.v2: Live since 2026-10-22. Before kick-off it combines each team’s recent results in every competition, its domestic league table and our league-strength coefficients (which make teams from different leagues comparable), and gives the current competition’s table more weight as the season goes on. In-play behaviour matches v1. Fixtures whose pre-match estimate was locked in before v3 still use it.
x-enumDescriptions.v3: Live since 2026-10-25. Pre-match it reuses v2, with two changes: a league match with a newcomer — a team that came into the competition by promotion or relegation, early in the season — uses only the current table and form, and the Turkish 1.Lig is now part of the league-strength coefficients. In play it applies v2’s formula plus a calibration step, phased in across the first 15 minutes, that makes the curve slightly less certain to correct a mild over-confidence.

x-enumDescriptions.kickoff: Kick-off: the pre-match estimate, placed at minute 0.
x-enumDescriptions.minute: The routine point emitted every minute; the estimate shifts as time runs down even if nothing else occurs.
x-enumDescriptions.goal: Emitted immediately after a goal; an own goal counts for the side it is credited to.
x-enumDescriptions.redCard: Emitted immediately after a red card, second yellows included.

PeriodKey.description: periodN: Regulation period number N. What a period is depends on the sport: a half in football, rugby, handball, futsal, minifootball and bandy; a quarter in basketball, American football and water polo; a period in ice hockey and floorball; a set in tennis, volleyball, table tennis, badminton and padel; an inning in baseball; a round in combat sports; a map / game in esports; a leg / frame block in darts and snooker. inningN: Cricket only: innings number N. extra1: Football and futsal: the opening half of extra time. extra2: Football and futsal: the closing half of extra time. overtime: Every overtime period summed into one value (American football, basketball, handball, ice hockey, water polo, …). In baseball it holds the runs scored in extra innings, and only when the source provides no inning-by-inning split (period10, …). penalties: The penalty shoot-out, which appears only as a `status.period` value; its score is kept in ScoreSide.penalties, not under a `periods` key.

Error.description: The body of every failed request. Branch on error.code; the message may be reworded.
